info.title: AuditManager PC-01 API
info.summary: The exact PC-01 journey: one project, one AR PDF, one text-consistency run, one CSV.
info.description:
Frozen at Gate A so `A5` can generate a typed client and `B6` can implement routers against a fixed shape, without either waiting on the other.

Resealed 2026-09-18 under owner ruling `R-3`: every operation here requires a bearer credential, declared once at the document root under `components.securitySchemes.bearerAuth`. The scheme names the seam and never its implementation. The operational liveness and readiness plane is outside `/api/v1`, carries no product meaning and needs no credential.

What this surface deliberately does not have: tenancy, WebSocket or server-sent events; an export resource, export identity or export polling, because a synchronous read creates nothing; and any endpoint outside the eleven capabilities `P2-API-01` enumerates, other than the credential exchange the authorization seam needs, which `W34-CONTRACT` adds below, the aggregate dashboard read `R-44` adds in `W46-SEAL`, further below still, and the account and registration operations `W49-SEAL-01` adds at the end. Roles and a per-client throttle on the unauthenticated registration operations were on this list until `R-55` and `R-56` ruled them in; the last reseal below says what each is.

Three rules hold everywhere and are not repeated per operation:

1. **Opaque identity.** Every identifier is `<prefix>_<ULID>` from `contracts/domain/v1/identifiers.json`, and every path parameter carries the pattern for its entity, with one exception: the portal block identity `portal_block_id` (`blk_` and 32 hexadecimal digits) is the portal's own value, carried verbatim, addressed only under a version and registered in the same file as an external identifier rather than as an identity. No response body, header or error detail ever contains a bucket name, object key, filesystem path, URL to internal storage, credential, prompt or model payload.
2. **One failure shape.** Every non-2xx response is the `ErrorEnvelope` of `contracts/domain/v1/error-envelope.schema.json`, its `error_code` drawn from the twenty-seven-code catalog and its `retryable` pinned to the catalog value for that code. A caller never infers retryability from the HTTP status.
3. **Correlation.** Every response carries `X-Correlation-Id`. A caller may supply one on the request; the edge assigns one when the caller does not.

Run state uses the contract vocabulary. The success terminal of an `AuditRun` is `published`. `succeeded` is a `StageResult` status on a different aggregate and never appears as a run state.

Resealed 2026-09-18 under owner ruling `R-5`, which closes `DEBT_REGISTER.md` `D-16` and `D-21` together. Three list operations -- `listDocuments`, `listVersions` and `listRuns` -- make published work reachable after a page reload: before them every read below the project list needed an identifier the client was already holding, so a reloaded screen could reach nothing that survived in the database and the store. And `RunStatus` gained `cost_micros`, `cost_basis` and `model_call_count`, so what a run spent is readable by a user for the first time. Each listing is a `GET` of the collection its parent creates into, pages with the same `cursor` and `limit` and returns the same `{items, page}` envelope as `listProjects`. No error code was added: an unknown parent is the catalog's `not_found` and a malformed cursor is `validation_failed`.

Amended 2026-09-18 under owner ruling `R-8`, which closes `DEBT_REGISTER.md` `D-18`. The domain catalog gains one code, `staged_upload_lost`, and the `ErrorCode` enum below carries it: twenty-one becomes twenty-two. Two blob-store failures demanding opposite operator responses -- *stop, the instance was restored wrong* against *retry the upload* -- both answered `conflict` with `aggregate_type` `Blob`, so their envelopes were byte-identical apart from `correlation_id`. A widened `safe_detail_keys` was offered and rejected, because a detail key cannot fix `retryable`: the envelope reads that flag from the catalog for the reported code, so only a separate code carries a separate value. **No path, operation or schema changed** -- that amendment moved none of the three counts -- and the new code travels on the `503` every staging write already declares.

Resealed 2026-09-22 by `W34-CONTRACT`. `R-3` declared the seam and left no way to get through it: the document required a bearer credential on every operation and described no operation that hands one out, so the only caller this surface admitted was one already holding a credential from somewhere the document does not name. One operation closes that -- `issueToken`, `POST /auth/token` -- and it is a credential *exchange* and nothing more: a login and a password in, an opaque credential and its lifetime out. It is the single operation whose `security` is the empty requirement, because requiring a credential to obtain one is a closed door with a handle on the inside.

**What this reseal deliberately did not add, because `T-6` forbade it.** No issuer, no discovery URL, no flow, no `bearerFormat`; and, until `R-55` superseded that part of `T-6` for the scope the `W49-SEAL-01` reseal below describes, no vocabulary of what a subject may do. The returned `token` is a string this document states no structure for; the deployment decides what it is, and the operations keep working when that decision changes. No error code was added either: an unaccepted login and password pair is the catalog's `authentication_required`, a malformed body is `validation_failed`. `permission_denied` is **not** declared here, because it means an authenticated subject refused a resource and this operation has no authenticated subject in it -- it is the operation that produces one. That reseal added one path, one operation and two schemas, and the sentence that stated the totals it produced has been rewritten as this delta: a reseal's own arithmetic stops being true at the next reseal, and `tests/contract/api_v1/test_surface_counts_in_prose.py` reads every such claim in this block against the live document. The totals are stated once, below.

Resealed 2026-09-22 by `W38-KB` under owner ruling `R-24`, which was ruled against the recommendation the owner was given: a client-side walk over runs and findings is cheaper and lives only as long as the alpha, and a listing operation costs a reseal and outlives it. One operation closes it -- `listDecisions`, `GET /decisions` -- because `listDecisionHistory` reads the history of **one** finding and nothing in this document enumerated decisions at all, so the knowledge base `R-23` requires had no source but a walk over every run. It is a projection in the sense `ADR-0012` fixes and creates nothing. Two component schemas were added, `DecisionRecord` and `DecisionRecordPage`; no parameter was, because `category` and `verdict` already exist and already mean the finding's category and the finding's current verdict. No error code was added: a malformed cursor is the catalog's `validation_failed`, an absent or refused credential is `authentication_required`, and there is no `404` on it at all -- the path addresses no parent identity, so an empty journal is an empty page. That reseal added one path, one operation and two schemas.

Resealed 2026-09-23 by `W39-REVOKE` under owner ruling `R-26`, which rules four account guards into the alpha. This is the one of them that **cannot be added later**: the other three make an account weak now and are fixed by adding them, while a credential already issued is permanent until it expires, and no later work reaches one sitting in somebody's browser. One operation closes it -- `changePassword`, `POST /auth/password` -- and it carries revocation with it, because the two share a mechanism: the account's credential generation is raised by the same write that stores the new digest, which is what makes every credential minted under the old password stop being accepted.

**What this does not add.** No response schema: a credential and its lifetime is one shape and `IssueTokenResponse` already names it. No error code: a wrong current password is the catalog's `authentication_required` and a new password that is the current one is `validation_failed`. No revocation operation: taking credentials away from accounts whose passwords nobody is changing is an operator's action on the deployment, and publishing it would have required deciding who may revoke whom, which this document then had no way to say. Since `W49-SEAL-01` an administrator's changes that take an account's rights away -- archive, a role change, a password reset -- revoke that account's credentials as part of the change, still without an operation of its own. One path, one operation and one schema. The surface moved to 15 / 18 / 51.

Resealed 2026-09-23 by `W42-SEAL` under owner rulings `R-37` and `R-29`, and it is the first reseal here that adds no path and no operation. **No path, operation or schema moved: still 15 / 18 / 51, exactly as before.** Three things change and each is a *description* or a *property of an existing schema*, which is precisely why it still costs a reseal -- the conformance gate drops descriptions as annotation under `N4`, so nothing but this document carries them to a reader, and `D-18`'s four documents move together or the frontend reads a contract the backend does not serve.

`R-37`, and `DEBT_REGISTER.md` `D-86`: `DecisionEvent.author_label` and `DecisionRecord.author_label` described themselves as *"one configured local reviewer label ... a label, not a subject identity"*. Since wave 41 that was false -- the server writes the authenticated reviewer, not a constant -- and the owner has now ruled that what it writes is the reviewer's **display name** rather than their login, because this is the field another reviewer reads on a decision somebody else took. **The schema does not move**: same type, same `minLength: 1`, same `maxLength: 128`. The sentence was wrong twice over and is corrected in both copies; `DecisionRecord` restates `DecisionEvent`'s properties rather than composing them with `allOf`, so a reseal that corrected one would have left `listDecisions` still describing the field falsely. An account that has chosen no display name records its login, which is a server-held string the reviewer typed and is 1..100 characters, inside this field's bounds by construction.

`R-29`, and `D-46`: `RunStatus` gains one optional property, `terminal_detail`. A `failed` run could say that a dependency was unavailable and could not say **which**, because the catalog's `safe_detail_keys` live on the `ErrorEnvelope` and a 200 run reading is not an error envelope. It is the same shape and the same rule as `ErrorEnvelope.details` -- safe scalar classifiers, restricted to the keys the domain catalog declares for the reported code -- applied to the code in `terminal_reason` instead of to the one in `error_code`, and it is present only beside a `terminal_reason` because the allowlist that bounds it is a property of that code. **No component schema was added**, because the shape is declared inline exactly as `ErrorEnvelope.details` is, and **no error code was added**: a distinct code for a replay miss was the row's other option and is a second reseal, which the owner did not take. The domain catalog did not grow in that reseal. The true sentence this makes sayable is *your document is fine, the provider is fine, this deployment has no recording for it*, which `R-30` made the ordinary case by putting the alpha stand in `recorded` mode. Two migrations carry the storage: `0009_reviewer_display_name` and `0010_run_terminal_detail`.

Resealed 2026-09-25 by `W45-BLOCKS`. One operation is added -- `getVersionBlocks`, `GET /versions/{version_uid}/blocks` -- the first half of `R-23`'s block markup: `page_geometry_extraction` writes a real `bbox` per extracted text line and this operation reads it back, keyed by `version_uid` rather than by `run_id` because the stage carries no model and no provider reference and its output is a deterministic property of the version, identical across every run that reaches it. It answers `404` for an unknown version and, for a known one, `status: "produced"` or `status: "not_produced"` -- absent is not empty, and a version whose geometry has not yet been derived answers the same `blocks: []` as one that genuinely has none, distinguished only by `status`. It carries no crops: the stage's second artifact, the page-crop manifest, is unconditionally empty in this pipeline and is not exposed here at all. Two component schemas are added, `VersionBlockIndex` and `BlockGeometry`; no error code was added, because the only refusal this operation needs, `not_found`, was already in the catalog.

Resealed 2026-09-25 by `W46-SEAL` under owner rulings `R-40` and `R-44` (`docs/program/OWNER_RULINGS_2026-09-17.md` section 3.15). Two things land together because `R-40` ruled both halves in, against the cheaper recommendation the drafting session gave: the field and its aggregation in one wave.

`UploadDocumentRequest.section` and `DocumentVersion.section` are added, both optional, drawing from the new `ProjectSection` enum -- legacy's fourteen project sections (`D-56`). The field lives on the document, not the version or the project: it classifies what a document is, not which revision of its bytes is being read, and a project holds many sections rather than being one. It is optional rather than required because this column starts with no rows to backfill and forcing every caller, `tests/e2e/**` among them, to name a section it may not know would fabricate a classification -- a document nobody has classified yet is a real state and is never defaulted to one of the fourteen.

One operation is added -- `getDashboardSummary`, `GET /dashboard` -- under `R-44`, the integrator's decision against the cheaper path: three of the four dashboard panels are already reachable by walking `listProjects`, `listDecisions` and `listRuns`, and the ruling is that the reseal this wave opens anyway should carry one aggregate read serving all four rather than three client-side walks a later aggregate read would only delete. It takes no parameter at all -- not a `project_uid`, not a date range, not a filter -- because a parameterised version of this operation would be a second, generic query surface over data three narrower operations already answer; what it answers is fixed: the operational shape of the whole deployment, right now. Every panel preserves absent is not empty: every `Verdict` and every `RunState` appears even at a count of zero, every one of the fourteen frozen sections appears in `section_breakdown` even with no documents, and the documents nobody has classified yet are their own row rather than folded into one of the fourteen. Seven component schemas are added -- `ProjectDocumentCount`, `VerdictCount`, `RunStateCount`, `RunActivitySpend`, `RunActivity`, `SectionDocumentCount` and `DashboardSummary` -- plus `ProjectSection`, eight in total. No error code was added: `getDashboardSummary` declares no `404`, because it names no parent identity to be missing, and no `422`, because it takes no parameter a caller could get wrong. That reseal added `/dashboard`, `getDashboardSummary` and the schemas named above.

Resealed 2026-09-29 by `W47-LOCK` under owner ruling `R-50` (`docs/program/OWNER_RULINGS_2026-09-17.md` section 3.17). `IssueTokenResponse` gains `is_default_credential`, boolean and required, answered by both operations that mint a credential. **No path, operation or schema moved**, because a property on a schema this document already carries adds no schema, and the domain catalog did not grow. That is why it is a reseal rather than an edit -- `D-18`'s four documents move together or the frontend reads a contract the backend does not serve.

**The owner took the expensive option on purpose, and this field is only half of it.** A deployment's seeded account is published in a migration's own docstring, so an unchanged password is a password everyone who has read the runbook already has. The field is the signpost: a client learns the state at the moment it signs in and can send that reviewer to a password screen. The lock is the other half and it is behaviour, not shape: while this field is `true`, every operation except `issueToken` and `changePassword` answers the `permission_denied` it already declares, carrying the detail key `required_capability` the domain catalog already permits it, with the value `password_changed`. **No error code was added and none was needed** -- naming the capability after the act rather than after the credential tells a caller what to do, and the credential already has a name in this response. A field without the refusal would leave the API open to the seeded password for any caller that skips the screens; a refusal without the field would leave the screens to discover the state by failing.

Resealed 2026-10-06 by `W49-SEAL-01` under owner rulings `R-55`, `R-56`, `R-59`, `R-60` and `R-61` (`docs/program/OWNER_RULINGS_2026-09-17.md` section 3.19). The alpha gains accounts a person can hold: an e-mail address as the sign-in identifier, a full name, a role set, registration requests an administrator decides, and account management. The operations named below are added with their paths and schemas, and the domain catalog gains one code and one safe detail key; no existing operation changes shape.

**Roles.** An account holds a set of `Role` values, `expert` and `admin`, and the server decides on every request what that set reaches -- a written register in the authorization seam, not a property of the credential and not a claim in it. Reading product data needs an active account with a complete profile and at least one role (`R-80`: an account whose role set is empty is suspended and reads only its own account, the product version and the release notes); product changes (projects, uploads, runs, verdicts, comments, the export) need `expert`; account and request management needs `admin`. A refusal is the `403 permission_denied` every guarded operation already declares, with `required_capability` naming what is missing: `password_changed` (`R-50`), `profile_completed` (an account that has not given its names and e-mail yet reaches only `getMe`, `updateMyProfile` and `changePassword`), `role:expert` or `role:admin`. A change of an account's rights -- a role change, an archive, a restore, an administrator's password reset -- revokes every credential it holds, so it signs in again before it meets the new rights.

**The account itself:** `getMe` and `updateMyProfile` (`R-59`: an account created before this reseal keeps its login until it gives its e-mail and names, in one write). **Registration:** `submitRegistration` and `readRegistrationStatus` are reachable without a credential, like `issueToken`; the status read shows an applicant `pending` and nothing else, and answers every other pair -- a rejected application included -- with the generic `401` (`R-56` and its addendum of 2026-10-06). `listRegistrations`, `approveRegistration` and `rejectRegistration` are an administrator's. **Management:** `listUsers`, `getUser`, `updateUser`, `archiveUser`, `restoreUser`, `purgeUser` and `resetUserPassword`, all `admin`; archive is the normal removal and purge deletes only an archived account that nothing references (`R-61`).

**The catalog.** `rate_limited` (`429`, retryable) is added because the edge in front of `/api/v1` now throttles the unauthenticated registration operations per client, and a code invented at the edge is what the catalog's safety rules forbid; this application never raises it, and it is not declared on the operations: like the edge's own body-size refusal, it is answered before any operation is reached. `conflict` gains the safe detail key `conflict_reason`, an enum-like classifier -- `login_taken`, `request_pending`, `queue_full`, `account_referenced`, `last_admin` -- so the account and registration conflicts can be told apart without a free-text detail. Identities `usr` and `reg` enter `contracts/domain/v1/identifiers.json`, and the `app_user` and `registration_request` machines enter `state-machines.json`, which is what `state_transition_not_allowed` names. The domain catalog gained `rate_limited` in W49 and `analysis_input_budget_exceeded` in W55b, and with later additions now carries twenty-seven codes.

Resealed 2026-10-08 by W52-SEAL-01: getProductVersion, listReleases and markReleaseNotesRead add the release boundary. That seal added the release operations and their shapes. All require an active complete account; a release read mark is the account's own state. The catalog and contract_version do not move. Stage C provides the release loader and runtime values.

W53-SEAL-01 adds durable execution declarations and optional RunStatus.reaudit_of_run_id. The seal declares the boundary; W53-EXEC-01 supplies behavior.

Resealed 2026-10-12 by W54-SEAL-01 under owner rulings R-80 and R-105. Two execution operations declare the worker registry of migration `0019_execution_workers`: `listWorkers` (`GET /execution/workers`, any one role, `role:admin|expert`) pages the registered workers with their state, intake, slots, version and current runs, and `setWorkerIntake` (`PUT /execution/workers/{worker_id}/intake`, `admin`, keyed by `Idempotency-Key`) stops or allows a worker taking new runs. Five component schemas and the `WorkerId` path parameter are added; identity `wrk` was already in the domain catalog. Both answer `503 dependency_unavailable` until W54-WORKER-01 supplies the registry; no error code is added and contract_version does not move.

Resealed 2026-10-12 by W55A-SEAL-01 under owner rulings R-80, R-112, R-113 and R-115 (plan `dispatch/W55-PLAN.md` section A3). Seven `norms` operations: `searchNorms` (`GET /norms/search`), `getNormDocument` (`GET /norm-documents/{norm_document_id}`), `listNormParagraphs` (`GET /norm-documents/{norm_document_id}/paragraphs`), `streamNormDocumentContent` (`GET /norm-documents/{norm_document_id}/content`, one `Range`) and `listNormSnapshots` (`GET /norms/snapshots`) for any one role, `role:admin|expert`; `listNormSnapshotEvents` (`GET /norms/snapshots/events`) and `setCurrentNormSnapshot` (`PUT /norms/snapshots/current`, a compare-and-set on `expected_current`, no `Idempotency-Key`) for `admin`. Migration `0020_norms_search` carries the one current snapshot, its append-only history and the search columns. `RunStatus` gains the optional `norms_snapshot_id` the run pinned. Twenty component schemas and the `NormDocumentId` path parameter are added; the identities `ns`, `ndoc` and `npar` were already in the domain catalog and a history row is an `evt` audit event. No error code is added (CD-19): refusals are `required_norm_unavailable` with `reference_kind` `norms_snapshot`, `norm_embedding_build` or `norm_source`, `conflict` with `conflict_reason: stale_current_snapshot`, and `validation_failed` with `constraint: norms_search_too_broad`. All seven answer `503 dependency_unavailable` until W55A-SEARCH-01; contract_version does not move.

Resealed 2026-10-13 by W55B-SEAL-01 under owner rulings R-80, R-116, R-117, R-118 and R-119 (plan `dispatch/W55-PLAN.md` section B3). `uploadDocument` takes a portal bundle: one ZIP holding the PDF, the portal's block list and its recognised-text markdown, and optionally the portal HTML (a digest only) and the stamp audit; a bare PDF is refused (`validation_failed`, constraint `portal_bundle_required`), and the limits become 500 pages and 250 MiB. Two `documents` operations read what a bundle brought, keyed by version like `getVersionBlocks`: `listVersionPortalBlocks` (`GET /versions/{version_uid}/portal-blocks`) pages the portal's blocks with their recognised text, quality flags and image descriptions, and `streamVersionPortalBlockCrop` (`GET /versions/{version_uid}/portal-blocks/{portal_block_id}/crop`) streams a PNG this product cut itself; both for any one role. Seven component schemas and the `PortalBlockId` path parameter are added; `portal_block_id` is an external identifier (`blk_` and 32 hexadecimal digits) and is registered beside the identities in `identifiers.json`, not among them. One error code is added, `analysis_input_budget_exceeded`: `startRun` and `reauditRun` refuse, before any run exists, a version whose text is larger than the analysis input budget (R-118). The bundle's constraint values and the busy refusal (`dependency_unavailable`, `dependency: upload_capacity`, with `Retry-After`) are registered in the domain catalog notes. `DocumentVersion.page_count` allows 500. Both new reads answer `503 dependency_unavailable` until W55B-GEOMETRY-01; contract_version does not move.

W56A-SEAL-01 adds optional AR v2 finding and decision fields, five categories, Severity, the model_identity_mismatch refusal and a caller-safe terminal message. The AR v2 recorded path that wrote those fields was removed by PROD-11-AR-V1-V2-REMOVAL-01; the fields, the five categories and Severity stay declared, and v1 responses omit the new fields.

Resealed 2026-10-20 by `W59-SECTION-SEAL-01` under owner rulings R-135 and R-139 and the design decision `W59-SECTION-IDENTITY-DECISION-01`. A version carries an explicit, expert-confirmed classification: its project stage (`ProjectStage`, `P` or `R`) and one of the fifteen sections. `ProjectSection` gains `PS`; migration `0011_document_section` keeps legacy's fourteen as the historical record and `0024_version_classification` stores the classification in its own append-only table outside the immutable version row. Two `documents` operations address one version through its document and project: `classifyDocumentVersion` (`PUT /projects/{project_uid}/documents/{document_uid}/versions/{version_uid}/classification`, `expert` only; an exact repeat keeps the first confirmer, a different choice is `conflict` with `conflict_reason: version_already_classified`) and `getVersionSectionReview` (`GET .../section-review`, any one role: the fifteen choices with display-only suggestion evidence, whether each has a registered text profile, and the current classification). `DocumentVersion` gains the optional `classification`. `startRun` and `reauditRun` route the analysis profile from the persisted classification and refuse an unclassified version or a section without a registered profile with `required_norm_unavailable` (`reference_kind` `version_classification` or `analysis_profile`; since `BETA-CONTRACT-SEAL-01` the dedicated codes `version_classification_required` and `section_profile_unavailable`, see the last reseal below); there is no AR fallback. Six component schemas are added; no error code is added and contract_version does not move.

Resealed 2026-10-20 by `W59-ANALYSIS-SETTINGS-01` under owner rulings R-135 and R-139. One `analysis` operation, `listAnalysisProfiles` (`GET /analysis/profiles`, any one role), lists the section-keyed text-profile registry that `startRun` and `reauditRun` route a classified version through: the fifteen sections in the project-structure order, each with its registered profile (`analysis_profile_id`, `prompt_bundle_id`, `profile_version`, `status` `draft`/`reviewed`, the prompt-bundle and profile hashes and, for a ported package, the legacy source repository, commit and files) or `null` when no profile is registered. Read-only: no operation edits a profile or changes its status. Six component schemas are added; no error code is added and contract_version does not move.

Resealed 2026-10-20 by `W59-DECISION-CARRYOVER-01` under owner rulings R-60, R-135 and R-139. `carryOverDecision` (`POST /projects/{project_uid}/documents/{document_uid}/versions/{version_uid}/comparison/carryovers`, `expert` only, keyed) carries one expert decision from a finding of the older version to the finding the recomputed comparison proposes as `unchanged`: the target receives one new `accept` or `reject` event authored by the confirming expert, whose comment records the carried-from finding, decision and versions; nothing else is written and nothing is carried without that confirmation. A refusal is `conflict` with `conflict_reason` `carryover_pair_not_proposed`, `carryover_source_decision_not_current`, `carryover_target_already_decided` or `carryover_severity_not_carryable`. `FindingComparison` gains the required `carryover_candidates`. Four component schemas are added; no error code is added and contract_version does not move.

Resealed 2026-10-20 by `W57B-NORMS-CATALOGUE-XLSX-01` under owner rulings R-135 and R-139. It adds `listNormDocuments` (`GET /norm-documents`, any one role) -- the current norms snapshot's documents as a catalogue with display names derived from the stored file names, filtered by text and kind, paged by a bound cursor -- and `exportRunXlsx` (`GET /runs/{run_id}/export.xlsx`, `expert`, as `exportRunCsv`) -- the run's W57b workbook with `exportRunCsv`'s states. Three component schemas are added: `NormCatalogueEntry`, `NormKindCount` and `NormCatalogueEntryPage`. No error code is added: the workbook's refusals are `storage_integrity_error` (`role: source.structured_companion`) and `required_norm_unavailable` (`reference_kind: norm_retrieval_set`), and contract_version does not move.

Resealed 2026-10-20 by `W61-DISPATCHER-01` under owner rulings R-60, R-135 and R-139 (roadmap Q-2). Four `dispatch` operations: `createAssignment` (`POST /assignments`, `admin`), `listAssignments` (`GET /assignments`, any one role; an expert reads only the assignments currently given to them), `getAssignment` (`GET /assignments/{assignment_uid}`, with the append-only history) and `transitionAssignment` (`POST /assignments/{assignment_uid}/transitions`: `started`, `completed`, `returned` by the current assignee holding `expert`; `reassigned`, `cancelled` by `admin`). The identity `asg_` is added to `identifiers.json` (entity `WorkAssignment`) and the `work_assignment` machine to `state-machines.json`; migration `0025_work_assignments` stores the assignment and its immutable event history. Ten component schemas are added; no error code is added (the refusal details are registered in `error-codes.json` notes) and contract_version does not move.

Resealed 2026-10-20 by `W60-PRICE-LIST-01` under owner rulings R-135 and R-139 and the roadmap's optimisation answers A-3 to A-5 (money only from an uploaded price list; a global vendor list per section, overridable per project, each change versioned). Six `optimisation` operations: `uploadPriceList` (`POST /projects/{project_uid}/price-lists`, `expert`, keyed, multipart: a CSV or an XLSX whose first sheet is read, at most 10 MiB and 20 000 data rows) stores the file as the project's newest immutable revision with its parsed positions and a deterministic parse report, every data row accepted or skipped with a reason and no price ever guessed; `listPriceListRevisions` (`GET /projects/{project_uid}/price-lists`) and `listPriceListPositions` (`GET /price-lists/{price_list_id}/positions`, offset paging, each unit price its exact decimal text) read them, any one role; `getEffectiveVendorLists` (`GET /projects/{project_uid}/vendor-lists`, any one role) answers all fifteen sections with the effective revision and both scopes' latest; `setGlobalVendorList` (`PUT /vendor-lists/{section_code}`, `admin`) and `setProjectVendorList` (`PUT /projects/{project_uid}/vendor-lists/{section_code}`, `expert`, mode `list` or `inherit`) append a revision or answer an exact repeat, and refuse a stale `expected_vendor_list_id` with `conflict_reason: vendor_list_changed`. The identities `prl_`, `prp_` and `vnl_` enter the domain catalogue (revision 16). No operation answers a total, a proposal or a price a price list does not state. These operations live here like every served operation; no separate optimisation contract family exists, and a future proposal pipeline would be a new family rather than part of this one. Twenty-seven component schemas are added; no error code is added and contract_version does not move.

Resealed 2026-10-20 by `W60-OPT-MATCH-01` under owner rulings R-135 and R-139. It adds `getSpecificationPrices` (`GET /projects/{project_uid}/documents/{document_uid}/specification-prices`, any one role, tag `optimisation`) -- «Спецификация и цены»: the specification rows of the document set's current version, read deterministically from its newest published run's saved text layer, each matched to the project's current price-list revision as `matched`, `ambiguous` or `unmatched` with its reason. The version must be classified by an expert (an `AR` version only until `OPT-PROJECT-ALL-SECTIONS-01`, any of the fifteen sections since); a precondition that does not hold is one `state` (`version_unclassified`, `price_list_missing`, `analysis_missing`, `text_unavailable`, `specification_too_large`; `section_not_ar` stays in the enum and is no longer produced) in a `200` answer, never an empty table. A price and an amount appear only on a row matched to exactly one position in the same unit with a numeric quantity; money is exact decimal text; totals are per currency over those rows only and every other row is counted by its one exclusion reason. Thirteen component schemas are added (`SpecificationPrices` and the twelve it is built from); no error code is added and contract_version does not move.

Resealed 2026-10-20 by `W60-OPT-PROPOSALS-01` under owner rulings R-60, R-135 and R-139 and the roadmap's optimisation answers A-2 to A-5 (a proposal is a separate entity beside findings with its own expert decisions, counts and export; the run records the vendor list it used; money only from matched price-list positions, absent rather than 0). Six `optimisation` operations: `startOptimisationPass` (`POST /projects/{project_uid}/documents/{document_uid}/optimisation-passes`, `expert`, keyed) pins the document set's current version, its newest published run, the current price-list revision and the effective vendor list of the version's section, and stores the deterministic proposals `cheaper_analog` (a cheaper position of the same price list, in the same unit and currency, from a vendor on the list, of the same kind of product; at most three per specification row), refusing an unclassified version, a missing price list, published run, saved text layer or vendor list with `conflict_reason` (a non-AR version was refused with `section_not_ar` until `OPT-PROJECT-ALL-SECTIONS-01`); `listOptimisationPasses` (`GET /projects/{project_uid}/optimisation-passes`), `listOptimisationProposals` (`GET /optimisation-passes/{optimisation_pass_id}/proposals`, offset paging, counts by decision, each saving an exact decimal text and absent when the row's quantity is not a plain number) and `listProposalDecisions` (`GET /optimisation-proposals/{optimisation_proposal_id}/decisions`) read them, any one role; `decideOptimisationProposal` (`POST /optimisation-proposals/{optimisation_proposal_id}/decisions`, `expert`, keyed) appends an `accept`, `reject` or `revise` (with a comment) decision, never changing an earlier one; `exportOptimisationProposalsCsv` (`GET /optimisation-passes/{optimisation_pass_id}/export.csv`) is the formula-escaped CSV of one pass, separate from the findings' CSV. The identities `opp_`, `opr_` and `opd_` enter the domain catalogue (revision 17); migration `0027_optimisation_proposals` stores the pass, its proposals and the append-only decisions. No finding is read or changed, and no model proposes anything: a model-assisted pipeline would be a new contract family. Eighteen component schemas are added; no error code is added and contract_version does not move.

Resealed 2026-10-20 by `W63-SECTION-FORM7-01` under owner rulings R-135 and R-139. It adds `getSectionSpecification` (`GET /sections/{section_code}/specification`, any one role, tag `optimisation`; optional `project_uid`, `q`, `offset`, `limit`) -- «Оптимизация разделов»: the Form-7 rows of every project whose document set's current version an expert confirmed in the section, each row priced from its own project's current price list. The section code is a filter, not an identity: every row carries its project, document set, version, page, sheet and line span, rows are never merged across projects, and totals exist per project and per currency only -- there is no section total. A project without a price list serves its rows with no match and no figure; a current version nobody classified is listed in `excluded`; one confirmed in another section never appears. A bound (projects scanned, member sets read, rows held) is a `200` answer with `state: section_too_large` and the bound's name, never a cut list. Six component schemas are added, built from the priced specification's own; no error code is added and contract_version does not move.

Resealed 2026-10-20 by `CLASSIFICATION-CORRECTION-01` under owner rulings R-135 and R-139. It adds `correctVersionClassification` (`POST /projects/{project_uid}/documents/{document_uid}/versions/{version_uid}/classification/corrections`, `expert` only, tag `documents`, `201`): an expert corrects a version's project stage and/or section by appending a numbered revision with a reason. Revision 1 is the original confirmation and is never changed; the current classification is the latest revision, and `VersionClassification` gains its `revision`. `expected_revision` is the optimistic-concurrency token and what makes a retry safe: an exact repeat answers the stored revision, a stale one is `conflict` (`classification_revision_stale`), an unclassified version is `conflict` (`version_not_classified`), a pair equal to the current classification is `validation_failed`. `SectionReview` gains `revisions`, the history, oldest first. Runs already started keep the analysis profile they pinned. Two component schemas are added (`CorrectVersionClassificationRequest`, `VersionClassificationRevision`); no error code is added and contract_version does not move.

Resealed 2026-10-20 by `NORM-REFS-RUN-01` under owner rulings R-135 and R-139. It adds `getRunNormReferences` (`GET /runs/{run_id}/norm-references`, any one role, tag `runs`) -- «Нормативные ссылки» on the run page: the normative documents the run's saved text cites (СП, ГОСТ, СНиП, СанПиН, ВСН, federal laws and government acts), each resolved against the norms snapshot the run pinned as `in_corpus`, `newer_edition`, `older_edition_only` (the corpus holds only an earlier edition than the one cited), `not_in_corpus` or `not_recognised`, with the pages each occurs on and the corpus document it points at. It is computed per request by the resolver the W57b rule uses, publishes no finding, proposes no severity and calls no model. A precondition that does not hold is a `200` with `state` (`snapshot_not_pinned`, `text_unavailable`, `too_many_citations`), never an empty list; the corpus documents whose designation the parser cannot read are listed as `unrecognised`, and pages without a text layer as `unread_pages`. An unknown run is `404`. Five component schemas are added; no error code is added and contract_version does not move.

Resealed 2026-10-21 by `BETA-CONTRACT-SEAL-01` phase A under owner rulings R-135, R-139 and R-141 and `D-179`. It adds no path, operation or schema and moves no contract_version. It adds two error codes, `version_classification_required` and `section_profile_unavailable` (both `422`, not retryable, no detail keys), the dedicated answers of the two run-start routing refusals of `startRun` and `reauditRun` that `W59-SECTION-SEAL-01` reported as `required_norm_unavailable` with `reference_kind` `version_classification` and `analysis_profile`. A caller that read those two `reference_kind` values reads the new codes instead; `required_norm_unavailable` keeps `reference_kind: analysis_profile` only for the executor's refusal of a run's pinned profile pair that the deployment does not register. Both refusals still precede the idempotency key's claim and write nothing. The `ErrorCode` enum has twenty-seven members.

Sealed 2026-10-21 by `BETA-CONTRACT-SEAL-01` phase B under owner rulings R-135, R-139 and R-141 and the integrator's closed-beta seal decision. contract_version moves from `1.0.0-draft.1` to `1.0.0` in this document (`info.version` and the `ErrorEnvelope` const), in the domain, analysis and events families together (`contracts/comparison/v1` is a README only), in every error body the application and the edge answer, and in what `getProductVersion` reports. The domain error catalog is `frozen` at twenty-seven codes. The surface is unchanged by this seal, and no error code is added. After this seal a change follows `VERSIONING_AND_FREEZE_POLICY.md`: an optional addition is a minor version, a clarification with no incompatibility a patch, and a removal, a rename or a change of meaning a major version or an explicit bridge. `OPEN-RETENTION` (`U-04`) stays undecided: the contract declares no retention window, time to live or legal-hold rule, and `idempotency_key_stale` names the fail-closed outcome without saying after how long. The edge's `rate_limited` (`429`) answers the credential exchange `issueToken` as well as the two registration operations, since `HARDEN-AUTH-EDGE-01`; like the edge's body-size refusal it is not declared on the operations. Two prose rules above are corrected: reading product data needs an account with a role (`R-80`), and the portal's `blk_` block identity is the one identifier that is not `<prefix>_<ULID>`. No `contracts/optimization/v1` family exists.

Resealed additively by `EXEC-SEAL-01` under owner rulings R-143 and R-144: the executor connections. New operations: `listExecutorConnections`, `createExecutorConnection`, `getExecutorConnection`, `reviseExecutorConnection`, `archiveExecutorConnection`, `setExecutorSecret`, `generateExecutorSshKey`, `requestExecutorProbe`, `listExecutorRoutes` and `setExecutorRoute`; the new component schemas are the `Executor*` family and its requests; `CostBasis` gains `unmetered`. A secret is write-only: no response, event or log carries one, and `setExecutorSecret` has no read counterpart. No error code is added; a refusal reuses `validation_failed`, `conflict`, `permission_denied` and `dependency_unavailable` with their existing detail keys.

Resealed additively by `EXEC-PULL-01` under owner rulings R-143 and R-144: the pull channel. New operations: `issueRunnerToken` and `revokeRunnerToken` (an administrator issues a runner token for a `pull` connection, shown once, and revokes it) and the four a runner calls with one: `claimExecutorTask`, `extendExecutorTaskClaim`, `submitExecutorTaskAnswer` and `failExecutorTask`. A runner token is a principal of its own, never a user session: it reaches those four operations and nothing else, and every other operation refuses it as `authentication_required`; the document declares the same `bearerAuth` scheme for them. `getExecutorConnection` gains the connection's runner tokens' metadata and its open task count. A runner's refusals use the existing error envelope: a declared model that is not the connection's pinned model is `422` with `error_code` `model_identity_mismatch`, and a refused answer keeps the claim. No error code is added. This pull reseal added runner operations and did not add the image transport.

Resealed by EXEC-IMAGE-DELIVERY-01 as 1.1.0: getExecutorTaskImage returns one bounded, verified PNG only to the token holding its current claim. ClaimedExecutorTask gains one optional image descriptor; old text tasks keep their shape. That seal added one runner PNG read and two schemas.

AR-V3-BETA-SIX-RUN-02 adds an explicit six-run beta group start and read. The start requires a server-installed reviewed pack and refuses before writing while none is installed. That seal added two group operations and four component schemas.

AR-V3-BETA-GROUP-API-SEAL-01 adds `getArV3BetaGroupReview`, a read-only six-scope projection of verified saved reviews. Pending, failed, verification-refused and available members remain distinct; provisional citations carry no numeric verdict. That seal added one operation and seven component schemas at contract 1.4.0.

AR-V3-BETA-PACK-STATUS-API-01 adds `getArV3BetaPackStatus`, a read-only report of whether a reviewed AR v3 beta pack is installed on this server and the reviewer attestation that came with its manifest. The attestation is a record the server shows; the response says nothing about whether it is true, and carries no map, set or snapshot identity. That seal added one operation and two component schemas at contract 1.5.0. No error code or migration was added.

EXEC-PAR-START-01 lets a run name its executor. `startRun` accepts an optional `executor_connection_id`; absent, the run follows the global route exactly as before. Present, the run freezes that connection's current revision when this release serves it, its current key has a passing probe and it is not archived, and otherwise the start is refused before any run exists: `422 validation_failed` (`field: executor_connection_id`) for an unknown or malformed id, `503 dependency_unavailable` (`dependency: executor_connection`) for a connection that cannot serve now. A named connection never falls back to the standby or to another connection, and the same idempotency key with another connection is `idempotency_key_reuse`. `reauditRun` keeps the original run's named executor. `RunStatus` gains a read-only, nullable `executor` (`RunExecutor`: connection, display name, pinned model) and nothing secret. No error code or migration is added.

PROD-11-AR-V1-V2-REMOVAL-01 removes АР v1 and v2 from the server. `startRun` and `reauditRun` on a version classified АР answer the existing `section_profile_unavailable` (no new error code: the catalog keeps its 27 codes), because АР is analysed only by the six-Run group (`startArV3BetaGroup`) and has no text profile; `listAnalysisProfiles` returns `profile: null` for АР. The enum `AnalysisProfileStatus` loses its member `builtin` (only the АР v1 profile carried it) and keeps `draft` and `reviewed`; the description of `reviewed` is corrected to say what the status is: a package whose open questions a lane answered in writing, with no human review (`R-146ag`). `FindingCategory` is unchanged. No path, operation or schema is added or removed. The contract version moves from 1.6.0 to 1.7.0 (a minor: no field, path or operation disappears, and the narrowing of `startRun` for АР is announced by an existing error code); no migration is added.

OPT-PROJECT-ALL-SECTIONS-01 opens «Спецификация и цены» (`getSpecificationPrices`) and the optimisation passes (`startOptimisationPass`) to a version an expert confirmed in any of the fifteen sections; they served an `AR` version only. The vendor list a pass pins is the effective list of the version's own section, and migration `0034_pass_scope_all_sections` makes the database hold the same rule (the pass's version and its vendor list must be of one section). The value `section_not_ar` of `SpecificationPrices.state` and of the pass `conflict_reason` stays and is no longer produced for a confirmed section; removing a value would be a breaking change. The description of `uploadDocument`, which still said that the analysis is built for AR and applied to any uploaded document, now describes the routing by the confirmed classification, and the description of `getDashboardSummary` says fifteen sections, not fourteen. No path, operation, schema, enum value or error code is added or removed. The contract version stays 1.7.0 (prose only).

COMPARE-PERSISTED-SUMMARY-01 makes the comparison of two versions a record. `approveSheetPairing` stores an expert's approval of one sheet pair that `compareDocumentVersions` proposed, and `withdrawSheetPairing` ends it with a new row; nothing is updated or deleted. Each is one write, with one audit event, in one transaction, idempotent by key and refused to an account without `expert` (`admin` alone is `permission_denied`). A sheet is a version, a page coordinate and the SHA-256 of the page text, never a display number. `compareDocumentVersions` gains `approved_pairs` (null for a refused comparison): the active approvals and, for approved pairs only, their deterministic line differences, recomputed from the immutable text and bound to the version bytes by a seal; the differences are withheld, never truncated, when a page's text has changed (`text_changed`), the seal differs (`seal_changed`) or the set exceeds the response budget (`too_large`). `generateComparisonSummary` is the only operation that calls a model about a comparison, and an expert asks for it once, on purpose: the command recomputes the sealed approved pairs, builds a bounded input from their changed lines (an input beyond the bound is refused, never shortened), checks the reply (every change it cites must exist; a reply that cites one that does not is stored as `rejected`, with no statements, because it was paid for), stores the summary append-only beside the raw differences, which it never alters, and passes its cost through the cost meter. `approved_pairs.summary` returns the newest stored summary with a fixed label saying that no human reviewed it; reading it calls no model. Only a recorded implementation exists (`provider_mode: recorded`, `cost_basis: unmetered`): a process in any other mode answers `503 dependency_unavailable` (`dependency: comparison_summary_model`), and a missing recording is `422 analysis_input_invalid`. New `conflict_reason` values: `sheet_pair_not_proposed`, `sheet_page_already_paired`, `sheet_pair_limit_reached`, `sheet_pair_too_large`, `approved_text_changed`, `sheet_link_not_active`, `comparison_not_available`, `summary_evidence_not_sealed`, `summary_input_empty` and `summary_input_too_large`. No error code is added and migration `0035_comparison_records` adds two tables. `ANALYSIS-PRESETS-01` (owner ruling `R-146av`) adds, under the same `1.8.0`, the named presets of how a run starts: `listAnalysisPresets` (any role), `createAnalysisPreset`, `reviseAnalysisPreset` and `archiveAnalysisPreset` (an administrator, keyed; revisions are append-only and an archive is a revision), the optional `StartRunRequest.preset_id` and the optional, nullable, read-only `RunStatus.preset`. A run start selects one setting per run, the executor connection, so a preset is a name and that connection: the cost ceiling is a process-wide setting and no threshold is an input of a start, so a preset holds neither. No error code is added; refusals use `validation_failed` (`unknown_preset`, `conflicts_with_executor_connection_id`, `unknown_connection`, `required`, `max_length`, `printable`, `differs_from_current`) and `conflict` (`preset_archived`, `preset_name_in_use`, `preset_limit_reached`, `connection_archived`) with their existing detail keys, and migration `0037_analysis_presets` adds one table and one nullable column of `audit_run`. `CMP-SEAL-C0` (wave C0 of the comparison modules, `ADR-0025`) adds, under `1.9.0`, the contract of the plain-PDF comparison upload, the order of the versions of a document set and the page reads, every operation a stub answering `503 dependency_unavailable` until its lane wires it. Twelve upload operations: `createComparisonUpload`, `listComparisonUploads`, `getComparisonUpload`, `getComparisonUploadProposal`, `uploadComparisonUploadPart` (a raw body of at most 16 MiB), `completeComparisonUploadFile`, `confirmComparisonUploadSet`, `excludeComparisonUploadSet`, `retryComparisonUploadSet`, `pauseComparisonUpload`, `resumeComparisonUpload` and `cancelComparisonUpload`; every write is keyed and an expert's act, the reads are any one role. `listComparisonVersionOrders` and `appendComparisonVersionOrder` read and append the order revisions of a document set (an append is an expert's act). `listVersionPageProfiles`, `getVersionPageProfile`, `streamVersionPagePreview`, `streamVersionPageThumbnail` and `streamVersionPageTile` read one page of one version from what the worker stored, addressed by the identity of the page's profile and never by a page number. `DocumentVersion` gains the optional `upload_kind` (`portal_bundle` or `comparison_pdf`); `ProductVersion` gains the optional `comparison_modules` (`none`, `versions` or `versions,stages`: the module set a deployment serves, `none` by default); `RunnerImage` no longer requires `portal_block_id` and may carry an opaque `crop_id`; `ClaimedExecutorTask.images` may hold up to eight images and `ClaimExecutorTaskRequest` may declare `max_images` (absent means one). No error code is added: the limits of an upload are refused as registered reasons under `validation_failed`, `conflict` and `storage_integrity_error`, and `comparison_only_version` is a reason under `analysis_input_invalid`. Migration `0038_comparison_foundation` adds nine tables. `CMP-SEAL-C1` (wave C1 of the comparison modules, `ADR-0025`) adds, under `1.10.0`, the contract of the version comparison core, every operation a stub answering `503 dependency_unavailable` until its lane wires it. The effective matrix of a document set: `getComparisonMatrix`, `prepareComparisonMatrix`, `applyComparisonMatrixEdits` (a keyed batch that carries the base matrix revision; a stale base is `409 conflict`), `undoComparisonMatrixEdit`, `listComparisonMatrixEdits` and `listComparisonAiLinks` (read-only here, written in wave C2). The series of adjacent transitions: `startComparisonSeries` («Запустить» and «Заново»), `listComparisonSeries`, `getComparisonSeries`, `pauseComparisonSeries`, `resumeComparisonSeries`, `cancelComparisonSeries` and `finishComparisonSeries` («Досчитать»), each transition with its summary counts and its deterministic verdict, and `listComparisonSheetPairs`, `getComparisonSheetPair` and `streamComparisonPairTile` for the sheet pairs of a transition (the eight channels, region classes, text changes with numbers, permit reconciliation and parts coverage; a tile of the overlay or of one page). `getComparisonOverview` reads the seven steps of every document set of a project and `getComparisonQueueSummary` the comparison work queue. Every write is keyed and an expert's act; the reads are any one role. `CreateComparisonUploadRequest` gains the optional `compare_after_preparation`. While the «Сравнение версий» module is on, `approveSheetPairing`, `withdrawSheetPairing` and `generateComparisonSummary` answer `503 dependency_unavailable` (`comparison_versions_module`): the effective matrix is the only store of sheet pairs of versions, and migration `0039` turned every active `0035` approval into a manual matrix edit. No error code is added: the new refusals are registered reasons under `conflict` (`comparison_matrix_stale`, `comparison_edit_none`, `comparison_series_state`, `comparison_series_active`) and `validation_failed`. Migration `0039_comparison_core` adds seven tables and two columns. `CMP-SEAL-C2` (wave C2 of the comparison modules, `ADR-0025`) adds, under `1.11.0`, the version comparison AI, specifications, launch queue and reports, every operation a stub answering `503 dependency_unavailable` until its lane wires it (and `comparison_modules` while the «Сравнение версий» module is off). The AI check of the doubtful pairs of a document set: `estimateComparisonAiPairCheck`, `startComparisonAiPairCheck`, `getComparisonAiPairCheck`, `pauseComparisonAiPairCheck`, `resumeComparisonAiPairCheck`, `cancelComparisonAiPairCheck` and `listComparisonAiPairHints`. The AI description of changes: per series `estimateComparisonAiSheetChanges`, `startComparisonAiSheetChanges`, `getComparisonAiSheetChanges` and the controls `pauseComparisonAiSheetChanges`, `resumeComparisonAiSheetChanges`, `cancelComparisonAiSheetChanges`, `finishComparisonAiSheetChanges` («Досчитать»), `dequeueComparisonAiSheetChanges` («Убрать из очереди») and `retryComparisonAiSheetChanges` («Повторить листы с ошибкой»); per sheet pair, or added or removed sheet, `getComparisonSheetDescription`, `listComparisonSheetDescriptionHistory`, `estimateComparisonSheetDescription`, `startComparisonSheetDescription` and `streamComparisonSheetDescriptionMd`; per transition `listComparisonReviewSheets`. Specifications: `getVersionPageSpecPositions` and `getComparisonSheetPairSpecPositions` (deterministic) and, for the AI comparison of whole specifications, `listComparisonSpecifications`, `getComparisonSpecification`, `listComparisonSpecificationChanges`, `estimateComparisonSpecification`, `startComparisonSpecification` and `cancelComparisonSpecification`. The launch queue: `getComparisonLaunchQueue`, `enqueueComparisonLaunch`, `pauseComparisonLaunchQueue`, `resumeComparisonLaunchQueue`, `clearComparisonLaunchQueue`, `removeComparisonLaunchEntry` and `getComparisonAiQueue`. The MD summary and the PDF reports: `streamComparisonSeriesSummary`, `createComparisonReport`, `uploadComparisonReportSource`, `listComparisonReports`, `getComparisonReport`, `startComparisonReport`, `cancelComparisonReport`, `continueComparisonReport`, `rebuildComparisonReportPdf`, `deleteComparisonReport`, `prepareComparisonClientReport`, `streamComparisonReportPdf` and `streamComparisonReportSourceMd`. Every AI start carries the estimate it consents to (the digest of an estimate in USD, the consent line, the ceilings of USD 10 per job and USD 50 per day for the installation, a pause when the actual spend passes 1.2 times the estimate, no limit for a connection that is not metered); every write is keyed and an expert's act; the reads are any one role. `ExecutorWorkKind` gains `comparison_pair_check`, `comparison_sheet_changes`, `comparison_spec` and `comparison_report`. Additive fields of the core: `ComparisonMatrixStaleReason` gains `algorithm_changed`, `ComparisonMatrixColumn` gains `label_source`, `ComparisonPairPage` gains `raster`; `startComparisonSeries` states the refusals `comparison_matrix_stale` and `comparison_versions_few`. No error code is added: the new refusals are registered reasons under `conflict`, `validation_failed` and `dependency_unavailable`. Migration `0040_comparison_ai_reports` adds twelve tables and widens the constraint of the executor routes. The C2 surface counts are recorded in `docs/program/CMP-SEAL-C2.md`. The contract version moved from 1.10.0 to 1.11.0 under `CMP-SEAL-C2` (a minor: operations, schemas and optional fields are added and nothing disappears). CMP-SEAL-C3 adds 32 typed stage-comparison operations: resumable PDF/ZIP intake, confirmed pairs and assemblies, sheet-map revisions, immutable raw text evidence and pinned seven-step runs. All new operations are stubs until their C3 lanes wire them; the module flag defaults to none. Migration 0041_comparison_stage_core adds fifteen tables. The surface is 204 paths, 230 operations and 570 schemas; 1.11.0 to 1.12.0 is additive.
CMP-SEAL-C4 adds 23 stage AI, repair, full chain/batch, cards, expert verdict and journal operations under 1.13.0. Migration 0042 adds twelve project-scoped tables and stage AI job scope. The C4 routes are module-gated typed stubs until their runtime lanes wire them.

post.summary: Exchange a login and a password for a bearer credential.
post.description:
The only operation on this surface that is reachable without a credential, because it is the one that hands one out: its `security` is the empty requirement, which overrides the document root for this operation and for no other.

**What this operation says about the credential it returns: nothing.** The response carries an opaque string and how long it stays valid. Its structure, what it encodes, and where the deployment got it are the deployment's own, are not described anywhere in this document, and are never parsed by a caller -- the same rule that keeps `bearerFormat` off `components.securitySchemes.bearerAuth`. A deployment that replaces a static string with something else changes no operation here.

Nothing is created and nothing is changed, so there is no idempotency key: a repeat of the same exchange is a second exchange, not a replay of the first. The edge in front of this surface counts the exchange per client address (six a minute, with a burst of ten) and answers `rate_limited` (`429`) itself, before the operation is reached; like the edge's own body-size refusal, that answer is not a response of the operation and is not declared here.

200.description: The credentials were accepted. The body carries the credential to present on every other operation and how long it stays valid.

post.summary: Change the signed-in account's password and revoke its old credentials.
post.description:
Two things happen here and they are one write. The account's password becomes the one supplied, and every credential this deployment ever minted for that account stops being accepted -- **including the credential this request presented**. A password change that leaves the old password's credentials working is a password change in name only, so the two are not offered separately and cannot land separately.

**Whose password changes is decided by the credential, never by the body.** There is no login property and there will not be one: the caller may change their own password and no other, and a login in the body would be an operation one caller could aim at another.

**The response is the replacement credential**, minted after the change, and the only one this account now accepts. It is answered rather than left to a second exchange because the caller's own credential was revoked by this very request: a `204` would leave them holding something already dead with no way to tell that from a failure.

The `403` is declared because every operation behind the seam declares it: `permission_denied` means an authenticated subject was refused, and a generated client needs a typed shape for it on every authorized operation. This operation does not raise it today: an account still on a default credential reaches it, so does an incomplete profile, and it needs no role.

Nothing is created, so there is no idempotency key. A repeat of the same request is refused by its own `current_password`, which is no longer current -- it is not replayed and there is no `409` here.

Revocation has no operation of its own on this surface. Ending a pilot -- taking credentials away from accounts whose passwords nobody is changing -- is an operator's action taken on the deployment; an administrator's changes that take an account's rights away (`archiveUser`, a role change through `updateUser`, `resetUserPassword`) revoke that account's credentials as part of the change.

200.description: The password was changed. Every credential minted for this account before this response -- including the one this request presented -- is refused from now on. The body carries the replacement.

201.description: The project was created, or the recorded outcome of an identical earlier request was replayed.

200.description: One page of projects.

post.summary: Upload one portal bundle and publish an immutable document version.
post.description:
The whole ingest path. The body is one portal bundle: a ZIP, recognised by its magic bytes whatever label the browser sends, holding exactly one `<stem>.pdf`, one `<stem>_blocks.json` and one `<stem>_results.md`, and optionally one `<stem>_results.html` (kept as a digest only: never stored, served or rendered) and one `<stem>_stamp_audit.json` (stored, and not used in analysis). All members share one stem. Anything else in the archive is refused, and so is any archive that is not what it claims to be (names that escape, links, encrypted members, a compression ratio above the bound, sizes beyond the bounds).

A bare PDF is refused with `validation_failed` and the constraint `portal_bundle_required`; the message says how to obtain the bundle. The PDF must be unencrypted and at most 500 pages, and the whole upload at most 250 MiB; every page must carry an embedded text layer or at least one portal block. Every refusal is `validation_failed` (or `storage_integrity_error`) with a `constraint` detail, and the registered values are in the domain error catalog (`error-codes.json`, `validation_failed`).

OCR is always marked: the portal's recognised text is kept as its own artifact with quality flags and is never merged into the PDF's text layer (R-116). The portal's descriptions of images are shown, marked, and never used in analysis (R-117). The upload runs no analysis. Which analysis a version gets is decided later, from the classification an expert confirms for it (`classifyDocumentVersion`, one of the fifteen sections): `startRun` routes the fourteen sections that have a registered text profile to their profile and refuses an unclassified version or a section with none, and АР is analysed only by the six-Run group (`startArV3BetaGroup`). A stated `section` here is the legacy label: it is stored and counted, it neither selects nor refuses an analysis, and it never makes a version classified (D-110, closed by W59-SECTION-SEAL-01).

A third upload in flight in one API process is refused before its body is read: `503 dependency_unavailable` with `details.dependency: upload_capacity` and a `Retry-After` header. Nothing was created; the caller sends the same upload again later.

On success the version and its input manifest are immutable: there is no update or delete endpoint for either, and the database refuses both. The manifest holds one entry per stored member: `source.document`, `source.structured_companion`, `source.markdown` and, when the bundle had one, `source.stamp_audit`.

201.description: A published, immutable document version.

get.summary: List the documents of one project, newest first.
get.description:
One item per document, carrying the version the document currently points at -- the one a reader would open, stream or start a run against. A document with no published version is not listed, because there is nothing to address.

The item is a `DocumentVersion` because that is what `uploadDocument` publishes into this same collection: the `GET` of a collection returns a page of exactly what its `POST` returns, which is the rule `listProjects` follows against `createProject`. This surface has no separate `Document` resource and does not acquire one here.

An unknown project is `404`, never an empty page: "this project has nothing in it yet" is a different answer from "there is no such project".

200.description: One page of this project's documents.

post.summary: Upload one portal bundle as the next immutable version of an existing document.
post.description:
The same ingest path as `uploadDocument`, into a document that already exists. The body is one portal bundle under exactly `uploadDocument`'s envelope (the same members, bounds, refusals and `constraint` details, a bare PDF refused with `portal_bundle_required`), and the same third-upload-in-flight refusal (`503 dependency_unavailable`, `details.dependency: upload_capacity`, `Retry-After`).

The new version gets the document's next `version_ordinal` and becomes its current version; every older version, its classification, runs, findings and decisions are unchanged. It inherits nothing: it takes no display title (the document keeps its own) and no section, and its `classification` is absent until an expert confirms one with `classifyDocumentVersion`. Two uploads into one document at the same time get consecutive ordinals.

An unknown project, an unknown document, or a document of another project is `404 not_found` (`details.aggregate_type` `Project` or `Document`), decided before the key is claimed or a byte is read into storage. The `Idempotency-Key` behaves as for `uploadDocument`: an exact repeat answers the version it created, and the same key with another document or another bundle is `409 idempotency_key_reuse`.

201.description: The next published, immutable version of the document.

200.description: The version and its input manifest.

get.summary: Stream the PDF bytes for the viewer.
get.description: The server streams the bytes itself. It does not redirect and does not return a presigned link: a URL into object storage is exactly the internal address the contract forbids putting in a response, and it would also outlive the request that authorized it.

parameters.name: Range
parameters.description: Byte range, so the viewer can page a large document without fetching all of it.

200.description: The complete PDF.

Content-Length.description: Byte size of the published version.

get.summary: List the runs of one published version, newest first.
get.description:
Runs hang off the version because `startRun` takes a `version_uid` and nothing else that identifies anything -- the project is derived from it. This is the inverse of that direction and not a second way of addressing a run.

Each item is the whole `RunStatus`, identical to what `getRunStatus` answers for that run. There is no lighter list shape: a second shape of one resource is a second thing to drift.

An unknown version is `404`, never an empty page.

200.description: One page of this version's runs.

get.summary: Read the page-by-page block index derived for one published version.
get.description:
Keyed by `version_uid`, not by `run_id`. `page_geometry_extraction` carries no model and no provider reference, so its output is a deterministic re-derivation of the source bytes and the published text layer -- identical across every run of this version that reaches the stage successfully. Addressing it by run would ask a caller to already hold a run identity to read a fact about the document.

An unknown `version_uid` is `404`. A version that exists but whose most recent successful run never reached `page_geometry_extraction` -- or has no run at all -- answers `200` with `status: "not_produced"` and `blocks: []`; that is a different fact from a version whose geometry was produced and genuinely has no blocks, which answers `200` with `status: "produced"` and `blocks: []`. The two are the same bytes for `blocks` and different bytes for `status`, and a caller reads `status` to tell them apart -- never the length of `blocks`.

This operation does not carry crops. `page_geometry_extraction` also publishes a page-crop manifest (`geometry.page_crops`); since `W55B-SEAL-01` it lists the crops this product cuts for the IMAGE blocks of a portal bundle under a non-empty `crop_policy`. That manifest and the portal blocks it describes are served by `listVersionPortalBlocks` and `streamVersionPortalBlockCrop`, not by this operation, which stays the text-line block index.

200.description: The block index for this version, or its not-yet-produced status.

get.summary: List the portal blocks of one published version.
get.description:
What the version's portal bundle brought, page by page: its blocks by type, the text the portal recognised in each TEXT block (marked `recognised`, with quality flags), the portal's description of each IMAGE block (marked, never used in analysis), and for each IMAGE block the crop this product cut itself. Keyed by `version_uid`, not by `run_id`, for the reason `getVersionBlocks` is: the geometry is a deterministic property of the version, read from the most recent run whose `page_geometry_extraction` succeeded.

An unknown `version_uid` is `404`. A version that exists but no run of which has produced portal geometry answers `200` with `status: "not_produced"` and no items; that is a different fact from a produced geometry that holds no blocks (`status: "produced"`).

Nothing here fetches, stores or serves a portal URL. Roles: any one role (`R-80`).

200.description: One page of the version's portal blocks, or its not-yet-produced status.

get.summary: Stream the PNG this product cut for one IMAGE block.
get.description: The server streams the bytes itself, with no redirect and no link. The image is the clip of the PDF page that the portal's block describes, rendered by this product and verified against its recorded SHA-256 before it is returned; it is never fetched from the portal. A version, a block or a crop that does not exist, a block that is not an IMAGE block, and a block on a page marked `geometry_mismatch` are all `404`: the caller's question is the same, there is no such image. Roles: any one role (`R-80`).

200.description: The PNG for this block.

get.summary: List the published versions of one document, newest first.
get.description:
Every immutable version of one document, ordered by `version_ordinal` descending. The ordinal is a display and ordering value and is never an identity; the continuation token carries the opaque `version_uid` and nothing else.

An unknown document is `404`, never an empty page.

200.description: One page of this document's published versions.

put.description: Classify one version: its project stage (`P` or `R`) and one of the fifteen sections, confirmed by the calling expert. `expert` is required; `admin` alone is refused with `permission_denied` (`required_capability: role:expert`). The version must belong to the named document and the document to the named project, otherwise `not_found`. An exact repeat answers the stored row and keeps the first confirmer; a different stage or section is `conflict` with `conflict_reason: version_already_classified` and changes nothing -- to change an existing classification an expert uses `correctVersionClassification`, with a reason. A suggestion, a file name or the legacy document `section` is never a classification.

200.description: The persisted classification, new or an exact repeat.

X-Correlation-Id.description: The correlation id for this request, assigned when the caller supplied none.

post.description: Correct one version's classification: append a new revision with the full target `project_stage` and `section_code`, a `reason` (1 to 2000 characters, with a letter or a digit) and the `expected_revision` the caller was looking at. `expert` is required; `admin` alone is refused with `permission_denied` (`required_capability: role:expert`). The version must belong to the named document and the document to the named project, otherwise `not_found`. Revision 1 is the original confirmation and is never changed; the current classification is the latest revision. An unclassified version is `conflict` with `conflict_reason: version_not_classified` -- classify it first. An `expected_revision` behind the current one is `conflict` with `conflict_reason: classification_revision_stale` and writes nothing, unless the request is an exact repeat (same expert, same values, same reason) of the revision after it, which answers that stored revision with `201` and writes nothing; one ahead of the current revision, a pair equal to the current classification (`constraint: differs_from_current`) and a blank, over-long or unprintable reason are `validation_failed`. Runs already started keep the analysis profile they pinned; a re-audit routes from the corrected classification. No `Idempotency-Key`: `expected_revision` is what makes a retry safe.

201.description: The revision this correction wrote, or the stored revision an exact repeat created.

X-Correlation-Id.description: The correlation id for this request, assigned when the caller supplied none.

get.description: The fifteen section choices for one version, each with the suggestion evidence its file name and recognised text carry (or `null`) and whether a text profile is registered for it (`executable`), plus the persisted classification or `null`, and the classification's history (`revisions`, oldest first: the original confirmation, then each correction with its expert, time and reason). Display input only: nothing here confirms a section or starts a run. Any one role, `role:admin|expert`.

200.description: All fifteen choices, their evidence and the current classification.

X-Correlation-Id.description: The correlation id for this request, assigned when the caller supplied none.

get.description: Compare two versions of one document set: the path names the older (source) version and `target_version_uid` the newer one. Both must be published versions of the named document in the named project with the same confirmed section and, with `mode=version` (the default), the same explicit project stage; with `mode=stage` the source must be classified `P` and the target `R` (design to working documentation of one set). Each needs a published run (the newest one, or the one `source_run_id` / `target_run_id` names). A path that names no such version is `404`; otherwise a pair the rule does not admit is `outcome: refused` with one `refusal.reason`, never relabelled. The answer carries proposed sheet pairs with their evidence, one page of raw line differences (`diff_offset`, `diff_limit`, `next_offset`) and proposed matches between the two runs' findings. Every pairing and match in `sheets`, `sheet_diffs` and `findings` is a proposal; this read writes nothing. `approved_pairs` (null for a refused comparison) lists the sheet pairs an expert approved for exactly this pair of versions (`approveSheetPairing`) and, for approved pairs only, their deterministic line differences, recomputed from the immutable text and bound to the version bytes by a seal; when a page's text is no longer the approved one (`text_changed`), the seal differs (`seal_changed`) or the set exceeds the response budget (`too_large`) the differences are withheld, never truncated. Any one role, `role:admin|expert`.

post.description: Carry one expert decision from a finding of the path's (older) version to the finding of `target_version_uid` that the comparison proposes as `unchanged`, on the calling expert's confirmation. The comparison is recomputed with the body's `mode` and runs when the confirmation arrives, and must still propose exactly this pair; the source finding's current verdict must still be the `source_decision_id` the expert was shown (`accepted` or `rejected`), and the target finding must have no decision event yet. The target receives one new `accept` or `reject` event authored by the caller, whose `comment` records the carried-from finding, decision and versions; a severity is carried with an accept or the carryover is refused, never dropped. Nothing else is written: the source finding and its decisions stay as they were. An exact repeat answers the event already carried, `replayed: true`, and keeps its first expert. A refusal is `conflict` with `conflict_reason` `carryover_pair_not_proposed`, `carryover_source_decision_not_current`, `carryover_target_already_decided` or `carryover_severity_not_carryable`. `expert` is required; `admin` alone is refused (`required_capability: role:expert`).
