X-Correlation-Id.description: The correlation id for this request, assigned when the caller supplied none.

post.description: Store the calling expert's approval of one sheet pair that the comparison of the path's (older) version with `target_version_uid` proposes: a source page and a target page of the two immutable versions, identified by the SHA-256 of their text and by `suggestion_sha256`, never by a display number. The comparison is recomputed with the body's `mode` and runs when the confirmation arrives and must still propose exactly this pair under this digest. The approval is one new row of an append-only history, with the actor, the time and the seal of the raw evidence of the approved set, and one audit event, in one transaction; it is never updated. An exact repeat of an active approval answers it, `replayed: true`. A refusal is `conflict` with `conflict_reason` `sheet_pair_not_proposed`, `sheet_page_already_paired`, `sheet_pair_limit_reached` (at most 32 active approvals), `approved_text_changed` (an earlier approval's page text is no longer the approved one; withdraw it first) or `sheet_pair_too_large`. `expert` is required; `admin` alone is refused (`required_capability: role:expert`). While the «Сравнение версий» module is on (`AUDITMANAGER_COMPARISON_MODULES` names `versions`) this operation answers `503 dependency_unavailable` (`details.dependency: comparison_versions_module`) and writes nothing: the effective matrix is the only store of which page of one version is which page of another (`ADR-0025` decision 13; migration `0039` turned the active approvals into manual matrix edits and kept the `0035` rows as history). With the module off it works as before.

post.description: End one active sheet link of the path's (older) version with a new row of the append-only history: nothing is updated or deleted, and the approval stays in the history. The body names the comparison view the expert was looking at (`mode` and runs): the approved set that remains is sealed over that view's text. A link that is not of this path is `404`; a link already withdrawn is `conflict` with `conflict_reason` `sheet_link_not_active`; a view that cannot be recomputed is `conflict` with `comparison_not_available`. The same key repeated answers the first withdrawal, `replayed: true`. `expert` is required; `admin` alone is refused (`required_capability: role:expert`). While the «Сравнение версий» module is on (`AUDITMANAGER_COMPARISON_MODULES` names `versions`) this operation answers `503 dependency_unavailable` (`details.dependency: comparison_versions_module`) and writes nothing: the effective matrix is the only store of which page of one version is which page of another (`ADR-0025` decision 13; migration `0039` turned the active approvals into manual matrix edits and kept the `0035` rows as history). With the module off it works as before.

X-Correlation-Id.description: The correlation id for this request, assigned when the caller supplied none.

post.description: Ask the model once, on purpose, for a summary of the approved sheet pairs of the path's (older) version and `target_version_uid`, and store the answer. This is the only operation that calls a model about a comparison; reading the comparison never does. The command recomputes the approved pairs' raw differences and their seal in its own transaction and needs them `sealed`; it builds the bounded input from the changed lines only (an input beyond the bound is refused, never shortened) and takes nothing from the client but the view. The reply is checked: every change it cites must exist; a reply that cites one that does not is stored as `rejected` (it was paid for) and returned as an answer, with no statements. The summary is stored append-only with the input digest, the prompt version, the provider mode and model identity, its statements and the span identities each cites; it never alters the raw differences, which the comparison returns exactly as computed, and it carries a fixed label saying no human reviewed it. The cost goes through the cost meter; in this release only the recorded implementation exists (`provider_mode: recorded`, `cost_basis: unmetered`), and a process in any other mode answers `503 dependency_unavailable` (`dependency: comparison_summary_model`). A missing recording is `422 analysis_input_invalid` and stores nothing. An exact repeat (same sealed input and prompt version, any key) answers the stored summary, `replayed: true`. A refusal before any call is `conflict` with `conflict_reason` `summary_evidence_not_sealed`, `summary_input_empty` or `summary_input_too_large`, or `comparison_not_available`. `expert` is required; `admin` alone is refused (`required_capability: role:expert`). While the «Сравнение версий» module is on (`AUDITMANAGER_COMPARISON_MODULES` names `versions`) this operation answers `503 dependency_unavailable` (`details.dependency: comparison_versions_module`) and writes nothing: the effective matrix is the only store of which page of one version is which page of another (`ADR-0025` decision 13; migration `0039` turned the active approvals into manual matrix edits and kept the `0035` rows as history). With the module off it works as before.

201.description: The stored summary of the approved pairs, new or an exact repeat.

X-Correlation-Id.description: The correlation id for this request, assigned when the caller supplied none.

post.summary: Start a text-consistency run over one published version.
post.description:
PD-03, in the subset PC-01 exercises. A new idempotency key creates a run. The same key with the same payload returns the existing run and creates nothing, whatever state that run is in, terminal included. The same key with a different payload returns `idempotency_key_reuse` and creates nothing. A new key over a terminal run creates a new run and leaves the terminal one exactly as it was: a terminal run is never reopened.

A version whose recorded text is larger than the most a run takes (the analysis input budget of one model call times the number of windows a run may use) is refused up front with `422 analysis_input_budget_exceeded` and no run exists (R-118). A version published before the portal-bundle upload has no recorded count and is not refused by this rule.

`W59-SECTION-SEAL-01`: the run's analysis profile is routed from the version's persisted classification through the section-keyed profile registry -- never from a file name, a suggestion or the document's legacy `section`, and never by an AR fallback. A version with no classification is refused with `422 version_classification_required`; a confirmed section with no registered text profile is refused with `422 section_profile_unavailable` (`BETA-CONTRACT-SEAL-01`, `D-179`: both used to be `required_norm_unavailable` told apart by `details.reference_kind`). Neither carries details, and both refusals precede the key's claim, so nothing is written. An existing run keeps the profile it pinned.

`EXEC-PAR-START-01`: the optional `executor_connection_id` names the connection the run must be on. Absent, the run follows the global route (and its standby rule) exactly as before. Present, the run freezes that connection's current revision if this release serves it, its current key has a passing probe and it is not archived; otherwise the start is refused before the key is claimed, so no run, command record or event exists: `422 validation_failed` with `details.field` `executor_connection_id` for an unknown or malformed id, `503 dependency_unavailable` with `details.dependency` `executor_connection` for a connection that cannot serve now. A named connection never falls back to the route's standby or to another connection. The choice is part of the payload the idempotency key is compared by: the same key with another connection is `idempotency_key_reuse`.

`ANALYSIS-PRESETS-01`: the optional `preset_id` names a saved preset instead of a connection. Its current revision is read in the start's transaction and its executor connection is applied exactly as if `executor_connection_id` had named it, so every refusal of that field applies unchanged; the run records the preset revision and `RunStatus.preset` shows it. `422 validation_failed` with `details.field` `preset_id` refuses an unknown preset (`unknown_preset`) and a preset together with `executor_connection_id` (`conflicts_with_executor_connection_id`); `409 conflict` with `details.conflict_reason` `preset_archived` refuses an archived one. All three precede the key's claim, so nothing is written. The preset, not the connection it resolved to, is part of the payload the idempotency key is compared by: a retry after an administrator revised the preset replays the run that exists, and the same key with a hand-chosen connection is `idempotency_key_reuse`. `reauditRun` records no preset.

202.description: The run exists. A replay under the same key and payload returns the same run and this same status.

get.summary: Read run state and per-stage state.
get.description: The polling target. `state` is the contract run state; `stages` carries one entry per stage the run scheduled, with the `StageResult` status vocabulary. A client stops polling on any terminal state.

200.description: Current run state.

get.summary: List the published findings of one run, with their evidence.
get.description: Published means grounded: every listed finding's quotations were verified present at their declared anchors. An ungrounded model item is not a finding, does not appear here and is retained only as run diagnostics.

200.description: One page of findings.

get.summary: Read one finding with its observation, evidence and provenance.

200.description: The finding detail.

post.description:
Append-only. Nothing is updated: an accept after a reject is a third event, and the current verdict is a projection over the stream. Replaying under one idempotency key appends exactly one event, which the database enforces rather than the handler promising it.

PC-01 emits `accept`, `reject` and `comment`. `revoke` is declared so the PD-01 revocation semantics stay implementable without a schema change; no PC-01 client offers it.

201.description: The appended event, and the projection that now follows from the stream.

get.summary: Read the decision history of one finding, oldest first.
get.description: Ordered by `(recorded_at, decision_id)`, which is a total order and is stable across pages. The server's row sequence is never exposed, in a field or inside a cursor.

200.description: One page of decision events.

get.summary: Read the decision journal across findings, newest first.
get.description:
Every expert decision this deployment has recorded, in one listing, with the finding context each event was recorded against. `listDecisionHistory` answers *what was decided about this finding*; this answers *what has been decided*, which no operation could answer before and which a client could otherwise reach only by walking every run and every finding.

**It is a projection and creates nothing.** `ADR-0012` holds: the current verdict, the reason aggregates and the knowledge-base views are rebuildable projections over the append-only ledger. Every property of `DecisionRecord` is rebuildable from `expert_decision_event`, `finding`, `finding_observation` and the `finding_current_verdict` projection, and this operation is the only place they are read together.

Ordered by `(recorded_at, decision_id)` **descending** - the newest decision first, as `listProjects` orders projects - and that is a total order, stable across pages. The server's row sequence is never exposed, in a field or inside a cursor.

`category` and `verdict` filter on the **finding**, exactly as they do on `listRunFindings`: the category of the finding the event was recorded against, and the verdict that now stands for it. Neither filters on the event. There is no parent identity in the path, so an empty journal is an empty page and never `not_found`.

200.description: One page of the decision journal.

get.summary: Download the CSV for one run.
get.description:
Synchronous. Nothing is created, so there is no export resource, no export identity and nothing to poll. Repeating the request returns byte-identical bytes.

The discriminator is the frozen `terminal_semantics.publishes_result` flag, not a hand-written state list (`OD-11`). A run whose terminal declares `publishes_result: true` - `published` or `partial` - is exported, with the degraded state carried explicitly in the `run_state` column rather than as a silent empty file. Every other state is refused with `state_transition_not_allowed`: a non-terminal run, and the terminal `failed`. `cancelled` is likewise not exportable and is unreachable in PC-01. `partial_result_not_publishable` is never emitted by this surface.

Bytes: UTF-8 with a byte-order mark, comma delimiter, CRLF line ending, RFC 4180 quoting. A text cell is written with one leading apostrophe when a spreadsheet could read it as a formula: when the first character that is not a space, a no-break space, a byte-order mark, a zero-width character, a tab, a carriage return or a line feed is `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` (or its fullwidth form), or when the cell itself starts with a tab, a carriage return or a line feed. Every other text is written as it is, an apostrophe is never doubled, and a number or a date is never touched (`SMALL-HARDENING-02`, `R-146ax`, `D-246`, `D-253`). The column list and its order are frozen in `docs/program/P02_SEAMS.md` section 6.

Synchronous, like `exportRunCsv`, and with its states and role: nothing is created, there is no export resource or identity, and repeating the request returns byte-identical bytes. An unknown run is `404`; a run whose terminal does not declare `publishes_result: true` is `409 state_transition_not_allowed`, decided on the run before anything else is read. A `partial` run is exported.

post.description: Starts the model work of a `draft` report: for the client kind one call per transition over the facts of the summary with discipline priorities, where a program check drops every point whose number, mark or direction the facts do not confirm; for the analytic kind an analyst, a verifier and a composer. The PDF is written by a program. The start carries the consent: the digest of the estimate that was shown and the explicit confirmation (`ADR-0025` decision 19). A digest that is not the one now computed is `409 conflict` (`comparison_estimate_stale`); a consent that is missing or not confirmed is `422 validation_failed` (`comparison_consent_required`); an estimate over the USD 10 ceiling of one job or the USD 50 ceiling of the installation's day is `409 conflict` (`comparison_ceiling_job`, `comparison_ceiling_day`), and a connection that is not metered has no ceiling; a live job for the same scope is `409 conflict` (`comparison_ai_job_active`); a work kind with no route in «Назначения» is `503 dependency_unavailable` (`executor_route_missing`). Nothing is sent to a model before the consent and the estimate agree, and the text of the answer is model output not confirmed by an engineer. A report that is not a draft is `409 conflict` (`comparison_report_state`). An unknown report is `404`. A keyed write: `Idempotency-Key` is required (`ADR-0025` decision 19). An expert's act (`role:expert`, `R-60`; an administrator without the expert role is refused). bearerAuth.description:
The authorization seam. Every operation in this document requires a bearer credential presented as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, except `issueToken`, `submitRegistration` and `readRegistrationStatus`, whose own `security` is the empty requirement: the credential exchange because it is what a caller with no credential uses to obtain one, and the registration pair because an applicant has no account yet.

**This declares the seam, not its implementation.** No issuer, no discovery URL, no flow and no token format appears here, and none may be added: the deployment decides them and the same operations must keep working when it does. What a subject may do is not carried by the scheme or the credential either: since `R-55` it is the account's role set (`Role`), which the server reads from the account on every request. `bearerFormat` is deliberately absent for that reason -- an opaque deployment token and an OIDC-issued JWT are both bearer credentials, and naming the format would pin the document to whichever one is current.

A request with no credential, or one the deployment does not accept, is `401 authentication_required`; so is an exchange whose login and password the deployment does not accept, which is the same refusal and not a second one. A credential the deployment accepts, for a subject not permitted this operation on this resource, is `403 permission_denied`, its `required_capability` naming what is missing (`password_changed`, `profile_completed`, `role:expert`, `role:admin`, or `role:admin|expert` where any one role suffices); authorization is decided server-side and the response never reveals the existence of a resource the caller may not see, so absence and refusal are reported as this surface's `404 not_found` where revealing them would leak.

Nothing outside `/api/v1` is covered. The operational liveness and readiness plane answers on its own port, carries no product meaning and needs no credential.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Client-supplied command key. Passed through to the owning command handler unchanged and never re-derived in the router. Never returned in a response body and never placed in an error envelope: it is a forbidden detail key.

CorrelationId.name: X-Correlation-Id
CorrelationId.description: Correlates this request with its diagnostic record. The edge assigns one when the caller does not supply it.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: Opaque continuation token from the previous page's `next_cursor`. Never parsed by a client and never constructed by one.

CategoryFilter.name: category
CategoryFilter.description: Restrict the page to one finding category.

VerdictFilter.name: verdict
VerdictFilter.description: Restrict the page to findings whose current projected verdict is this value.

RegistrationStatusFilter.name: status
RegistrationStatusFilter.description: Restrict the page to requests in this status.

CorrelationId.description: Present on every response, success or failure, so an operator can find the diagnostic record without the response carrying unsafe content.

AuthenticationRequired.description: `authentication_required`. No valid authenticated subject was presented: the request carried no bearer credential, or one this deployment does not accept, or -- on the credential exchange, which presents no credential by design -- a login and password pair this deployment does not accept. The response carries no hint about the addressed resource, so it is the same answer whether or not the resource exists.

PermissionDenied.description: `permission_denied`. The authenticated subject is not permitted to perform this operation on this resource. Authorization is decided server-side. This is the caller's rights and nothing else: a dependency that refuses the *application's* own credential is `dependency_credential_refused` on the 500 response, which is a server fault and not this one.

NotFound.description: The addressed aggregate does not exist or is not visible. The response never reveals the existence of a resource the caller may not see.

ValidationFailed.description: The request or payload violates a declared schema, enum, format or invariant. Nothing was created or changed.

UploadRejected.description: The upload failed the portal-bundle envelope (`validation_failed`) or its bytes did not match their declared checksum or size (`storage_integrity_error`). In both cases nothing was published: no version row, no manifest and no readable object.

StorageIntegrityError.description: Stored bytes do not match their declared identity.

RunInputInvalid.description: The declared analysis inputs are not structurally acceptable (`analysis_input_invalid`), the request itself is invalid (`validation_failed`), or the version's text is larger than the most a run takes: the analysis input budget of one model call (derived from the configured model and the per-run cost ceiling) times the number of windows a run may use (`analysis_input_budget_exceeded`, with `details.character_count` and `details.budget_characters`), or the version's analysis profile cannot be routed: it has no expert-confirmed stage and section (`version_classification_required`) or its confirmed section has no registered text profile (`section_profile_unavailable`). Nothing was created in any case.

IdempotencyConflict.description: One of: `idempotency_key_reuse`, the same key with a different payload, which creates and changes nothing; `idempotency_key_in_progress`, the same key and payload still executing, which the caller retries under the same key and never re-issues under a new one; `idempotency_key_stale`, the recorded outcome is no longer available and is not guessed; or `conflict` for a uniqueness invariant with no more specific code.

RunNotExportable.description: `state_transition_not_allowed`. The run's terminal does not publish a result - a non-terminal run, or the terminal `failed` - so there is no download. A `partial` run is exported and is never refused here.

InternalError.description: An unclassified server fault, a declared run failure, or `dependency_credential_refused` -- a dependency refusing the application's own credential, which is a server-side configuration fault with no authenticated subject in it. The original internal code stays in protected diagnostics and never reaches this envelope.

DependencyUnavailable.description: `dependency_unavailable`, or since `R-8` `staged_upload_lost` on a write that stages bytes. The caller retries; nothing was partially applied. `idempotency_key_in_progress` is also retryable and is reachable on every write, so a caller reads `retryable` from the envelope, where the catalog pins it per code, and never infers it from the status or from a description like this one.

StateConflict.description: The change conflicts with durable state. `conflict` carries `details.conflict_reason`: `login_taken` (an active account holds the login), `request_pending` (a request for the login is already pending), `queue_full` (the pending queue is at its cap of 100, or 40 requests that are pending or approved were submitted within the last rolling 24 hours), `account_referenced` (the account is referenced and cannot be purged) `last_admin` (no active account would hold `admin`) or, on `setCurrentNormSnapshot`, `stale_current_snapshot` (the current norms snapshot is no longer the one the caller named in `expected_current`), or, on `classifyDocumentVersion`, `version_already_classified` (the version already holds a different stage or section; the first classification stands). `state_transition_not_allowed` names the `app_user` or `registration_request` machine with `details.machine`, `current_state` and `requested_state`. On the executor operations (`EXEC-SEAL-01`), `conflict_reason` is `connection_archived` (the connection is archived), `connection_routed` (a route still names the connection) or `no_revision` (the connection has no revision yet). On an operation that takes an idempotency key the idempotency-key codes are reported here too.

ApprovalConflict.description: One of: `idempotency_key_reuse`, `idempotency_key_in_progress` or `idempotency_key_stale`, as on every keyed create; `state_transition_not_allowed` against `registration_request` when the request is no longer pending (of two concurrent approvals one wins and the other gets this); or `conflict` with `details.conflict_reason: login_taken` when an active account took the login meanwhile, which leaves the request pending.

FindingUid.description: Durable semantic issue identity, carrying expert history across reruns.

FindingObservationId.description: Immutable evidence emitted by exactly one run.

CorrelationId.description: Not an entity identity. Never a foreign key and authorizes nothing.

CostBasis.description: How well a published cost figure is known. `measured` means every provider call the figure sums reported its own cost; `estimated` means at least one did not, so the total is derived; `unmetered` (`EXEC-SEAL-01`, `R-143f`) means a call ran on a connection that has no per-call cost, so the figure is absent and never a zero. The value is an aggregate over **every** call the figure spans and is never the last call's basis: a run whose first attempt replayed and whose second reported a cost is `estimated`.

IdempotencyKey.description: Not an entity identity. Never interpreted as, converted into or stored as a system identifier.

Sha256.description: A verification value, never an identity.

Cursor.description: Opaque pagination token. It encodes the sort key of the last item on the page and nothing else; it is never a database row number or sequence value.

next_cursor.description: Token for the next page, or null when this is the last page.

ErrorCode.description: Exactly the key set of contracts/domain/v1/error-codes.json.

ErrorEnvelope.title: ErrorEnvelope
ErrorEnvelope.description: The one failure shape. Rendered by ``envelope_response`` and by nothing else.

RunState.description: The audit_run states of contracts/domain/v1/state-machines.json. The success terminal is `published`; there is no `succeeded` run state. `created` is transient and rarely observed by a client. `cancelled` is declared by the contract and is unreachable in PC-01, which has no cancel command.

StageStatus.description: StageResult statuses from contracts/analysis/v1. A `succeeded` stage carries no error; every other status carries one.

StageId.description: A canonical stage identity from contracts/analysis/v1/stage-registry.json. PC-01 schedules the first four.

ArV3BetaStageId.description: Profile-specific AR v3 beta review stage; the legacy nine-stage registry is unchanged.

ProviderMode.description: Whether the model call was made live or replayed from a recording. Visible in the UI and in the CSV, because a recorded run is not evidence of a live one.

Verdict.description: The current projected verdict. `pending` when the ledger holds no verdict-bearing event, and after a revocation. `needs_manual_review` is declared for the closed union and has no PC-01 producer.

inferred from a file name, and never the analysis ``stage_id``, which is why the property

ClassifyDocumentVersionRequest.description: `W59-SECTION-SEAL-01`. An expert's explicit stage and section for one version.

CorrectVersionClassificationRequest.title: CorrectVersionClassificationRequest
CorrectVersionClassificationRequest.description:
`CLASSIFICATION-CORRECTION-01`. An expert's correction of one version's classification.

The full target pair, why, and the revision the caller was looking at
(``expected_revision``): the optimistic-concurrency token that also makes an exact retry
safe. At least one of the two values must differ from the current classification.

VersionClassification.title: VersionClassification
VersionClassification.description:
`W59-SECTION-SEAL-01`. The persisted, expert-confirmed classification of one version.

The original confirmation is stored once (``0024_version_classification``) and never
changed. `CLASSIFICATION-CORRECTION-01` (``0028_classification_corrections``): an expert
may append corrections, each a numbered ``revision`` (1 is the original); this is the
latest revision, or, in the answer to a correction retried after someone corrected again,
the revision that request created. ``confirmed_by_user_uid`` and ``confirmed_at`` are those
of **that revision** -- who stands behind these values.

VersionClassificationRevision.title: VersionClassificationRevision
VersionClassificationRevision.description:
`CLASSIFICATION-CORRECTION-01`. One entry of a version's classification history.

Revision 1 is the original expert confirmation (``reason`` is ``null``); revisions 2..
are the corrections, each with the expert who made it, when, and why. Never changed.

SectionReview.title: SectionReview

DiffHunk.title: DiffHunk
DiffHunk.description:
One span of a raw line diff; 0-based line indices, end exclusive. An ``equal`` span
carries its ranges and no lines.

ApprovedDiffHunk.title: ApprovedDiffHunk
ApprovedDiffHunk.description:
One span of an approved pair's raw line diff; 0-based line indices, end exclusive. A
changed span carries ``hunk_id`` (``<sheet_link_id>:<n>``, ``n`` counting the sheet's
non-equal spans from 0); an ``equal`` span carries its ranges and neither lines nor an id.

ApprovedSheetDiff.title: ApprovedSheetDiff
ApprovedSheetDiff.description: The deterministic differences of one approved pair, recomputed on every read.

ApprovedSheetPair.title: ApprovedSheetPair
ApprovedSheetPair.description: One active expert approval of a source page against a target page.

ApprovedSheetPairs.title: ApprovedSheetPairs
ApprovedSheetPairs.description:
`COMPARE-PERSISTED-SUMMARY-01`. The active approvals of the compared pair and their
deterministic evidence. ``evidence_state``: ``none`` (no active approval), ``sealed`` (the
differences were recomputed and their seal equals the stored one), ``text_changed``,
``seal_changed`` or ``too_large`` (no difference is served, none is truncated).

SummaryStatement.title: SummaryStatement
SummaryStatement.description:
`COMPARE-PERSISTED-SUMMARY-01` (B2). One statement of a summary and the changed spans of the
approved pairs it cites, each ``<sheet_link_id>:<n>`` (``n`` counts the sheet's non-equal spans
from 0), the same identities ``ApprovedDiffHunk.hunk_id`` carries.

ComparisonSummary.title: ComparisonSummary
ComparisonSummary.description:
`COMPARE-PERSISTED-SUMMARY-01` (B2). A model's summary of the approved pairs, stored beside
their raw differences and never inside them. ``label`` is fixed and shown with it: no human has
reviewed the text. ``state`` is ``ready`` or ``rejected`` (the check refused the reply: no
statements, one ``rejection_reason``; the reply was paid for, so it is recorded). ``provider_mode``
``recorded`` is a replayed reply, ``model_identity`` ``recorded`` then, and ``cost_basis``
``unmetered``. ``is_current``: it describes the approved set as it stands now.

CarryoverCandidate.description:

CarryOverDecisionRequest.title: CarryOverDecisionRequest
CarryOverDecisionRequest.description:

The path names the source (older) version; the comparison is recomputed with these
values when the confirmation arrives. ``source_decision_id`` is the decision the expert
was shown: if the source's current verdict has moved on, nothing is carried.

CarryOverDecisionResponse.title: CarryOverDecisionResponse
CarryOverDecisionResponse.description:
`W59-DECISION-CARRYOVER-01`. The carried event on the target finding and where it
came from. ``replayed`` is true when the target already carried exactly this event (an
exact repeat): nothing was appended and the first confirmation stands.

ApproveSheetPairingRequest.title: ApproveSheetPairingRequest
ApproveSheetPairingRequest.description:
`COMPARE-PERSISTED-SUMMARY-01`. One expert confirmation of one proposed sheet pair.

The path names the source (older) version; the comparison is recomputed with these values
when the confirmation arrives and must still propose exactly these pages under exactly this
``suggestion_sha256``.

WithdrawSheetPairingRequest.title: WithdrawSheetPairingRequest
WithdrawSheetPairingRequest.description:
`COMPARE-PERSISTED-SUMMARY-01`. The comparison view the withdrawing expert was looking at:
the text the remaining approved set is sealed over is that view's text.

SheetPairingEvent.title: SheetPairingEvent
SheetPairingEvent.description:
`COMPARE-PERSISTED-SUMMARY-01`. The stored approval or withdrawal of one sheet link.
``replayed`` is true when this call appended nothing: the same key repeated, or an exact
repeat of an active link under another key.

GenerateComparisonSummaryRequest.title: GenerateComparisonSummaryRequest
GenerateComparisonSummaryRequest.description:
`COMPARE-PERSISTED-SUMMARY-01` (B2). The comparison view the expert is looking at; the
command recomputes the sealed evidence in its own transaction and takes nothing else from the
client: not the input, not the model, not the seal.

GenerateComparisonSummaryResponse.title: GenerateComparisonSummaryResponse
GenerateComparisonSummaryResponse.description:
`COMPARE-PERSISTED-SUMMARY-01` (B2). The stored summary, new or an exact repeat
(``replayed``: nothing was called and nothing was appended).

BlockGeometry.description: One derived block, one extracted text line. `block_id` is an anchor inside this artifact -- it matches `Evidence.block_id`'s pattern -- and is never a contract identifier.

block_ordinal.description: Position of this block within its page, starting at 0.

bbox.description: Points, top-left origin, y increasing downward -- see `bbox_unit` and `bbox_origin` beside it.

char_start.description: Document-global offset into the version's prepared text layer, counted in Unicode code points -- the same sequence `Evidence.char_start` indexes.

VersionBlockIndex.description: The page-by-page block markup derived for one version. Carries no crops: `page_geometry_extraction` also publishes a page-crop manifest, and this pipeline renders no visual detection, so that manifest is unconditionally empty and is a separate artifact this operation does not expose.

status.description: `produced`: a run reached `page_geometry_extraction` and this is its output, `blocks` may still be empty for a version that genuinely has none. `not_produced`: no run of this version has published this artifact yet -- absent, not empty -- and `blocks` is `[]` for that reason instead.

produced_by_run_id.description: The run whose `page_geometry_extraction` result this is. Null exactly when `status` is `not_produced`.

text_layer_sha256.description: Binds this block index to the exact prepared text layer its spans index. Null exactly when `status` is `not_produced`.

block_count.description: `len(blocks)`, carried rather than left for a caller to recompute.

provider_mode.description: Defaults to the server's configured mode. A client asking for `live` is asking to spend money; the OD-03 ceiling applies unless relaxed_limits is true.

executor_connection_id.description: EXEC-PAR-START-01: the executor connection this run must be on. Absent: the run follows the global route exactly as before. Present: that connection's current revision is frozen when this release serves it, its current key has a passing probe and it is not archived; otherwise the start is refused and no run exists. Never replaced by the route's standby or by another connection. Part of the payload the idempotency key is compared by.

preset_id.description: ANALYSIS-PRESETS-01: a saved preset (listAnalysisPresets) to start the run with. Absent: the run is what it was. Present: the preset's current revision is read in the start's transaction and its executor connection is applied exactly as if executor_connection_id had named it (same usability test, same refusals, no fallback to the standby or to another connection), and the run records the preset revision. Exclusive with executor_connection_id. Part of the payload the idempotency key is compared by, as the preset and not as the connection it resolved to.

relaxed_limits.description: Temporary section-analysis option. Absent or false keeps the deployment cost ceiling and a 16,000-token output request. True omits the per-Run cost halt and requests up to 64,000 output tokens under a distinct immutable profile and bundle identity. The 12-window operational document-size limit remains. The provider may enforce a lower output maximum. The choice is part of the idempotency payload and persists for the Run.

cost_consent.description: The expert confirms a fresh estimate and a sufficient explicit ceiling before this start may spend. The approved cap applies independently of the raised output-limit choice.

error_code.description: The typed reason a non-succeeded stage carries. Null exactly when the status is `succeeded`.

RunExecutor.description: EXEC-PAR-START-01: which executor a run is on. Identity, display name and pinned model only; never a secret, an address or a probe.

norms_snapshot_id.description: W55A-SEAL-01 (R-113, CD-6): the norms snapshot this run pinned when it was created -- the current snapshot at that moment. Absent while no snapshot is current, which until W57 is the expected state of every run.

degradation_set.description: The explicitly recorded missing or degraded stage set. Non-empty exactly when the run is `partial`; a `published` run carries none.

terminal_reason.description: The catalog code a `failed` run terminated with. Null otherwise.

terminal_detail.description: D-46: safe scalar classifiers saying WHICH dependency a `failed` run terminated on, restricted to the `safe_detail_keys` the domain catalog declares for the code in `terminal_reason`. Present only beside a `terminal_reason`, because the allowlist that bounds these keys is a property of the reported code; absent when there is nothing to say, and never an empty object. The same shape and the same rule as `ErrorEnvelope.details`, applied to a 200 run reading rather than to a failure -- which is why it had to be added at all: a run reading is not an error envelope and carried no detail object. It classifies; it never identifies. No path, object key, URL, credential, token, prompt, payload or host appears here, and no error code was added to the catalog for it.

terminal_message.description: Caller-safe typed stage failure message; absent on v1 and on runs without a typed failure. Never contains a proxy body, URL, credential, prompt or model payload.

interrupted_reason.description: OD-10: a run left `running` by a crash is reconciled to `failed` with an explicit interrupted reason. There is no `interrupted` state.

diagnostic_observation_count.description: Ungrounded model items rejected by the grounding gate. They are not findings and appear in no finding list.

cost_micros.description: What this run spent at the provider, in millionths of the provider currency unit, as an integer. Never a floating-point money value. It is the sum of `cost_micros` over **every** `model_call` row of this run, including every retry attempt, because the per-run budget ceiling is enforced over the same span. Absent when the run made no provider call at all, which is a different fact from a cost of zero.

model_call_count.description: How many provider calls `cost_micros` sums. Published rather than left to be inferred: a reader who cannot see it cannot tell a run answered first time from one that was retried, and the two spent differently. Present exactly when `cost_micros` is.

norm_retrieval_set_id.description: The verified retrieval set frozen for this v3 run; absent for v1/v2. It must belong to norms_snapshot_id.

executor.description: EXEC-PAR-START-01: the executor the run froze at start, read-only: the connection, the name an administrator gave it and the model its frozen revision pins. Null (and omitted) for a run that froze no connection. Nothing about the connection's kind, address, key or probe.

preset.description: ANALYSIS-PRESETS-01: the preset revision the run was started with, read-only: the preset, the revision number and the name it had then. Null (and omitted) for a run started without a preset, which includes every re-audit.

Evidence.description: One verified quotation. `char_start` and `char_end` index the document-global character sequence of the prepared text layer, counted in Unicode code points after the declared normalization - see docs/program/P02_SEAMS.md section 4.

block_id.description: Secondary anchor into this version's block index. Not a contract identifier.

ObservationProvenance.description: What produced this observation. Checksums and identities only: never the prompt, the request or the response body.

norm_citations.description: A certified v3 citation partition. An empty array means the CITE gate completed and persisted a checked count of zero; absence on v1/v2 means no certification, never zero.

required_value.description: Deterministically grounded normative requirement; absent for legacy and nonnormative observations.

stated_value.description: Document value grounded in the project evidence; absent for legacy and nonnormative observations.

Finding.description: A published finding. Every listed finding is grounded: its quotations were verified present at their declared anchors.

norm_citations.description: A certified v3 citation partition. An empty array means the CITE gate completed and persisted a checked count of zero; absence on v1/v2 means no certification, never zero. On Finding and FindingDetail this mirrors the canonical observation.

required_value.description: Deterministically grounded normative requirement; absent for legacy and nonnormative observations. Mirrors the canonical observation.

stated_value.description: Document value grounded in the project evidence; absent for legacy and nonnormative observations. Mirrors the canonical observation.

FindingDetail.description: One finding with its full current-verdict projection. Restates `Finding` rather than composing it with `allOf`: under JSON Schema 2020-12 an `additionalProperties: false` is evaluated against its own schema object's property annotations only, so an `allOf` branch over the closed `Finding` would reject the two properties the sibling branch adds. Both shapes stay closed, and tests/contract/api_v1 asserts this property set stays `Finding`'s plus exactly `latest_comment` and `decision_event_count`.

latest_comment.description: The comment of the most recent event carrying one, whatever its type.

norm_citations.description: A certified v3 citation partition. An empty array means the CITE gate completed and persisted a checked count of zero; absence on v1/v2 means no certification, never zero. On Finding and FindingDetail this mirrors the canonical observation.

required_value.description: Deterministically grounded normative requirement; absent for legacy and nonnormative observations. Mirrors the canonical observation.

stated_value.description: Document value grounded in the project evidence; absent for legacy and nonnormative observations. Mirrors the canonical observation.

finding_observation_id.description: The observation the expert actually reviewed. A verdict is recorded against the evidence in front of the reviewer, not against whatever the newest run later produced.

comment.description: Required for `comment`; optional on any other event type.

DecisionEvent.description: One appended event. Never updated and never removed.

verdict.description: The verdict this event carries, or null for a comment.

author_label.description: OD-12, as `R-37` now defines it: the display name of the reviewer who recorded the event -- the name they chose, or their login when they have chosen none -- derived server-side from the authenticated credential and **never** taken from a request body. It IS a subject identity: it names which reviewer judged, which is what `P04` needs and what one configured label for every reviewer could not give it. It still authorizes nothing: it is what the ledger records about who judged, not a permission anybody holds, and no client can choose it. The ledger is append-only, so an event keeps the label it was written with even after that reviewer is renamed.

DecisionRecord.description: One event of the decision journal, with the finding context it was recorded against. A rebuildable projection and never a source of truth: every property here is derived from `expert_decision_event`, `finding`, `finding_observation` and the `finding_current_verdict` projection, and nothing is stored in this shape. It restates `DecisionEvent`'s properties rather than composing them with `allOf`, for the reason `FindingDetail` states: under JSON Schema 2020-12 an `additionalProperties: false` is evaluated against its own schema object's property annotations only, so an `allOf` branch over the closed `DecisionEvent` would reject the properties the sibling branch adds.

verdict.description: The verdict this event carries, or null for a comment.

author_label.description: OD-12, as `R-37` now defines it: the display name of the reviewer who recorded the event -- the name they chose, or their login when they have chosen none -- derived server-side from the authenticated credential and **never** taken from a request body. It IS a subject identity: it names which reviewer judged, which is what `P04` needs and what one configured label for every reviewer could not give it. It still authorizes nothing: it is what the ledger records about who judged, not a permission anybody holds, and no client can choose it. The ledger is append-only, so an event keeps the label it was written with even after that reviewer is renamed.

finding_text.description: The observation's own words, as `FindingObservation.finding_text` carries them. It is the analysis's text and not this API's prose, so it is in whatever language the analysis produced.

decision_event_count.description: How many events the ledger holds for this finding, including this one. A count greater than one means the expert returned to the finding.

login.description: The caller's login, spelled the way the deployment spells it. Not an identity of this surface: it addresses nothing, appears in no path and is never a foreign key.

password.description: The secret presented with the login. It appears in no response body, no error detail and no diagnostic record.

token.description: The credential, presented on the authorized operations as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Opaque: this document states no format for it, and a caller that reads anything out of it has taken a dependency this contract does not offer.

expires_in.description: How long the credential stays valid, in seconds counted from this response. A lifetime and never a clock reading, so no clock has to agree between the two sides. A caller exchanges again before it elapses; an elapsed credential is `authentication_required` like any other the deployment does not accept.

is_default_credential.description: Whether the account this credential was just minted for is still on the password the deployment seeded it with. `true` says the password has never been changed; `false` says it has. It is a fact about the account's password and not a statement about what the subject may do -- what follows from it is declared where refusals are declared: every operation but this one and `changePassword` answers `permission_denied` with `required_capability: password_changed` while it is `true`. Required, not optional, because a caller that could not read it would have to assume a value and the only assumable value is the permissive one.

current_password.description: The password the account holds now, proved before anything is changed. It appears in no response body, no error detail and no diagnostic record. A value that is not this account's is `authentication_required` -- the same refusal a missing credential gets, because 'this deployment does not accept this' is one fact.

new_password.description: The password the account will hold. The bounds are mechanical. The deployment enforces a password policy on this operation — a refusal is `validation_failed` and names the rule in `message` — and that policy is not declared here, because it is the deployment's and may differ between them. No history and no expiry are enforced. A value equal to `current_password` is `validation_failed`, because a change that changes nothing would report a password as changed when it was not.

ProjectDocumentCount.description: One row of the "documents per project" panel: the same fact `Project.document_count` already publishes, gathered for every project in one read.

VerdictCount.description: How many findings, across every project, currently stand at one verdict. Every member of `Verdict` is present -- a verdict nobody has recorded is `count: 0`, not an absent row.

RunStateCount.description: How many runs, across every project, currently sit in one state. Every member of `RunState` is present, for the same reason `VerdictCount` states.

RunActivitySpend.description: What every run, across every project, has spent at the provider so far. `cost_basis` is `measured` only when every contributing `model_call` row reported a measured cost.

spend.description: Absent when the deployment has made no provider call.

SectionDocumentCount.description: How many published documents carry one project section (`R-40`, `D-56`). `section` absent means this row is the unclassified bucket, not a sixteenth section. Every one of the fifteen current codes is present even at `document_count: 0`.

section.description: One of the fifteen project sections, or absent when the document has not been classified.

DashboardSummary.description: `getDashboardSummary`'s whole answer. All four panels, one read, no filter.

UserUid.description: Opaque account identity. An e-mail address is the sign-in identifier and a unique key among active accounts; this is the identity every reference names.

Role.description: One role an account may hold; an account holds a set of them (R-55, R-60). `expert` makes product changes -- projects, uploads, runs, verdicts, comments and the export. `admin` manages accounts and registration requests. Reading product data needs one of them (R-80): an active account whose role set is empty is suspended and reads only its own account, the product version and the release notes.

RegistrationStatus.description: The states of the `registration_request` machine in `contracts/domain/v1/state-machines.json`: `pending` until an administrator decides, then `approved` or `rejected`, both terminal.

Account.description: One account, as the account itself reads it through `getMe` and an administrator reads it through the account operations. No credential material.

login.description: The sign-in identifier: the normalised e-mail address (trimmed, lower-case, ASCII, an internationalised domain in its `xn--` form, at most 254 characters) once the profile is complete, or the legacy login an account created before the identity upgrade keeps until it completes its profile. Not an identity of this surface.

display_label.description: The name to show for this account, resolved by the server and never empty: the name form `Last F. M.` when the account has a last and a first name, else the display name an operator chose, else the login. A complete profile always has the name form (R-55).

last_name.description: Null until somebody gives the names.

first_name.description: Null until somebody gives the names.

middle_name.description: Optional; null when the person has none.

roles.description: The role set, sorted. Empty is a valid set: such an account reads product data and changes nothing.

profile_complete.description: False for an account that has not given its names and e-mail yet. Such an account reaches only `getMe`, `updateMyProfile` and `changePassword`; every other operation answers `permission_denied` with `required_capability: profile_completed`.

is_default_credential.description: True while the account must change its password: it is still on the password the deployment seeded it with, or an administrator reset it. The same fact `IssueTokenResponse.is_default_credential` reports at sign-in.

archived_at.description: Null for an active account. An archived account cannot sign in and none of its credentials is accepted; an administrator may restore it.

PersonNames.description: A person's names, set together. 1-60 characters of letters, separated by single spaces, hyphens or apostrophes, with no word mixing Cyrillic and Latin letters. Surrounding whitespace and invisible characters are removed before the rule is applied.

middle_name.description: Optional; absent when the person has none.

UpdateMyProfileRequest.description: The signed-in account's own names, and -- while its profile is incomplete -- the e-mail address that becomes its login. 1-60 characters of letters, separated by single spaces, hyphens or apostrophes, with no word mixing Cyrillic and Latin letters. Surrounding whitespace and invisible characters are removed before the rule is applied.

middle_name.description: Optional; absent when the person has none.

email.description: Required to complete a profile whose login is not yet an e-mail address; it becomes the login in the same write that stores the names. A complete profile's login is fixed: an `email` other than the current login is `validation_failed` with `details.field: login`.

UpdateUserRequest.description: An administrator's change of an account's names, its role set, or both. An absent property leaves that half unchanged.

roles.description: The whole new role set, not a delta. Removing a role from oneself is `permission_denied`; leaving no active account holding `admin` is `conflict` with `details.conflict_reason: last_admin`.

temporary_password.description: The password the account signs in with next and must then change. It is held to the deployment's password policy against the account's login, and it appears in no response body, no error detail and no diagnostic record.

SubmitRegistrationRequest.description: An application for an account. 1-60 characters of letters, separated by single spaces, hyphens or apostrophes, with no word mixing Cyrillic and Latin letters. Surrounding whitespace and invisible characters are removed before the rule is applied.

login.description: The applicant's e-mail address, which becomes the account's login on approval. Normalised by the server (trimmed, lower-case, ASCII, at most 254 characters).

password.description: The account's future password, held to the deployment's password policy with the applicant's names and e-mail local part added to its blocklist. Stored hashed until the decision, which removes it; it appears in no response body, no error detail and no diagnostic record.

middle_name.description: Optional; absent when the person has none.

RegistrationStatusResponse.description: What an applicant is told: that the application is pending. This is the only status this surface ever shows an applicant (R-56 and its addendum of 2026-10-06); a decided application is answered like an unknown pair.

RegistrationRequest.description: One registration request, as an administrator reads it. No credential material.

login.description: The normalised e-mail address the applicant gave.

display_label.description: The applicant's name form, `Last F. M.`, resolved by the server.

middle_name.description: Null when the applicant gave none.

decided_at.description: Null while the request is pending.

decided_by.description: The administrator who decided; null while pending.

rejection_reason.description: The administrator's reason, present only on a rejected request. It is read by administrators only and is never shown to the applicant.

created_user_uid.description: The account an approval created. Null while pending, on a rejected request, and after that account was purged.

RegistrationRequestPage.description: One page of requests and the number of pending requests in all, whatever the filter -- the administrator's badge.

roles.description: The roles the new account receives: at least one.

reason.description: Why the request is rejected, 1-256 characters after surrounding whitespace is removed, with no control character but a line feed. Stored for administrators; the applicant is not shown it.

ReleaseNoteKind.description: The editorial category of a release note.

ReleaseNoteItem.description: One user-facing note; where is the navigation label saved at release time.

ReleaseEntry.description: The highest stored revision of one visible release. The archive entry is last; range_label is null for a normal release.

ReleaseList.description: Visible releases newest first, archive last, and the versions this account has not yet read.

MarkReleaseNotesReadRequest.description: The known release version through which this account has read. Unknown or future versions are refused.

WorkerState.description: The state of one registered worker, derived from its last heartbeat (W54-SEAL-01, plan section 3.6): `online` while it heartbeats, `stale` after 90 seconds without a heartbeat, `offline` after 600 seconds.

ExecutionWorker.title: ExecutionWorker
ExecutionWorker.description: One row of the worker registry (`worker`, migration `0019_execution_workers`) and the runs it currently holds. `intake_enabled` false means it takes no new run.

NormBuildState.title: NormBuildState
NormBuildState.description: The snapshot's ``bge-m3-dense-v1`` build (D-127) over its reliability-aware chunks.

NormDocument.title: NormDocument
NormDocument.description:
One document of a snapshot. ``content_available`` is true exactly when its PDF has a
confirmed custody binding, which is the only way ``streamNormDocumentContent`` serves it.

NormCatalogueEntry.title: NormCatalogueEntry
NormCatalogueEntry.description:
One document of the current snapshot as the catalogue lists it
(`W57B-NORMS-CATALOGUE-XLSX-01`). ``designation`` and ``title`` are derived for display
from the stored file name and are never identities; ``title`` is null when the name
carries nothing after the designation. ``kind`` is the stored document type verbatim.

NormCatalogueEntryPage.title: NormCatalogueEntryPage
NormCatalogueEntryPage.description:
One page of the catalogue; ``total`` counts the documents the filters keep and
``kinds`` lists every kind of the snapshot with its document count.

NormFragment.title: NormFragment
NormFragment.description:
`NORM-Q01`. A plain-text excerpt of the canonical paragraph text, with the matched
spans as offsets rather than markup.

NormHighlight.title: NormHighlight
NormHighlight.description: One matched span of a fragment, as character offsets into ``NormFragment.text``.

NormParagraphPage.title: NormParagraphPage
NormParagraphPage.description: One document's canonical paragraphs in ``ordinal`` order, and its attribution.

NormSearchHit.title: NormSearchHit
NormSearchHit.description: One reliable canonical paragraph of the searched snapshot.

NormSnapshot.title: NormSnapshot
NormSnapshot.description:
One loaded snapshot. ``qualified`` is the setter's own predicate (a complete build
and a confirmed source binding for every document's PDF); ``current`` marks the one
current snapshot.

NormSnapshotEvent.title: NormSnapshotEvent
NormSnapshotEvent.description: One row of the append-only history of the current snapshot, newest first.

NormSourceAttribution.title: NormSourceAttribution
NormSourceAttribution.description:
`NORM-Q04`. Where a norm document's text came from, carried exactly on every norms
response. The corpus is internal (D-4.1); nothing here is a publication claim.

NormTextReliability.title: NormTextReliability
NormTextReliability.description:
F-4. An ``unreliable`` paragraph's recognised text did not survive repair; it is
shown marked in a document view and is never a search result.

SetCurrentNormSnapshotRequest.title: SetCurrentNormSnapshotRequest
SetCurrentNormSnapshotRequest.description:
``expected_current`` is the snapshot the caller believes is current, ``null`` when it
believes none is; a stale belief is ``conflict`` (``stale_current_snapshot``).

PortalBlockId.description: An external identifier: minted by the portal that produced the bundle and carried verbatim from its block list (`blk_` and 32 lowercase hexadecimal digits). It is not an identity this product generates, and it addresses a block only together with a `version_uid`.

PortalBlockType.description: The portal's own block types, lower-cased. A `stamp` block exists only in the block list: the recognised-text markdown never carries one.

PortalGeometryState.description: The page-box check. `geometry_mismatch` means the portal's page size and the PDF's page box disagree beyond the frozen tolerance: no crop was cut for that page, and its blocks are shown without one rather than with a wrong one. The stage still reports success.

PortalCrop.description: A crop this product cut itself from the PDF with a clip render. It is never the portal's `crop_url`, which is a capability URL and is neither fetched, stored nor served. The bytes are `streamVersionPortalBlockCrop`; `sha256` is theirs.

PortalRecognisedText.description: The portal's OCR text of a TEXT block. It is always marked `recognised` (R-116): never merged into the PDF text layer. `flags` are the quality signals found in it, a lowercase snake_case vocabulary: mixed-script words, Latin/Cyrillic homoglyphs, CJK characters, doubled list markers and the norms degeneracy signals. Engineering designations (`1.A`, `B25`, `A500C`, `REI 150`) are exempt. `text` is markdown and is rendered as text, never as HTML.

PortalBlock.description: One block of the portal's block list. The pair `(version_uid, portal_block_id)` addresses it. `page_number` is the true 1-based PDF page; `page_label` is the portal's own integer label, kept. `ordinal` is the portal's order on the page: not unique, and null for a stamp. `bbox_norm` is `[x0, y0, x1, y1]` in the page's normalised top-left space, each in [0, 1]; `polygon_points`, when the portal gave a polygon, are its `[x, y]` vertices. `crop` exists only for an IMAGE block on a page whose `geometry` is `ok`. `recognised_text` exists for TEXT blocks the markdown holds; `portal_description` is the portal's text for an IMAGE block, shown marked and never used in analysis (R-117). An absent optional member is omitted, never null.

PortalBlockPage.description: One page of a version's portal blocks, ordered by `page_number`, `ordinal` (null last) and `portal_block_id`; the continuation token carries that key and nothing else. `status` is the distinction `VersionBlockIndex.status` carries: `not_produced` is a version no run of which has produced portal geometry yet; `produced` is one whose geometry stage succeeded and which may genuinely hold no blocks. `block_count` is the whole version's, not the page's. A caller reads `status`, never the length of `items`.

NormRetrievalSetId.description: Verified immutable retrieval-set identity; never a display label or corpus filename.

UngroundedReason.description: Closed deterministic observation-withholding reasons; a withheld item is never a published finding.

NormCitation.description: One persisted, verified citation to a labelled paragraph in the run-pinned snapshot and retrieval set. A rebound preserves the cited label and identifies the one matching paragraph. Never inferred from a display designation.

NormObservationCitationPartition.description: One canonical or merged observation with its independently certified citation partition. A zero partition is explicit, never inferred from an empty SQL result.

norm_citations.description: A certified v3 citation partition. An empty array means the CITE gate completed and persisted a checked count of zero; absence on v1/v2 means no certification, never zero.

NormFindingVerification.description: Citation partitions of one published finding; canonical and member observations are proved separately.

NormVerificationReport.description: Read-time report for a v3 run only. A v1/v2 run is not found. A partial v3 run still reports its typed stage error; no unverified or uncertified partition is exposed. textless_pages is context only and never citation evidence.

AnalysisProfileStatus.title: AnalysisProfileStatus
AnalysisProfileStatus.description:
`W59-ANALYSIS-SETTINGS-01`. Where a registered text profile stands.

``draft``: a package ported from the legacy prompts, or authored in this repository, whose
open questions no lane has answered in writing. ``reviewed``: a package whose open questions a
lane answered in writing; no human review (`R-146ag`). Every status is executable; the status is
recorded, never hidden. АР has no status because it has no text profile
(`PROD-11-AR-V1-V2-REMOVAL-01`): its row carries ``profile: null``.

AnalysisProfileSourceFile.title: AnalysisProfileSourceFile
AnalysisProfileSourceFile.description: One legacy file a package's prompt was ported from, with its SHA-256.

AnalysisProfileSource.title: AnalysisProfileSource
AnalysisProfileSource.description: The legacy repository, commit and files a package's prompt was ported from.

AnalysisProfileSummary.title: AnalysisProfileSummary
AnalysisProfileSummary.description: One registered text profile: its identities, version, status and content hashes.

AnalysisProfileListItem.title: AnalysisProfileListItem
AnalysisProfileListItem.description: One section and its registered profile, or ``null`` when none is registered.

AnalysisProfileList.title: AnalysisProfileList
AnalysisProfileList.description: All fifteen sections, in the project-structure order, each with its profile or ``null``.

AssignmentStatus.title: AssignmentStatus
AssignmentStatus.description:
`W61-DISPATCHER-01`. An assignment's status, derived from its latest event.

``assigned`` (after ``assigned`` or ``reassigned``), ``in_progress`` (``started``),
``done`` (``completed``), ``returned`` and ``cancelled``. ``done`` and ``cancelled`` are
terminal.

AssignmentEventKind.title: AssignmentEventKind
AssignmentEventKind.description: `W61-DISPATCHER-01`. One event of an assignment's append-only history.

AssignmentTransitionKind.title: AssignmentTransitionKind
AssignmentTransitionKind.description: `W61-DISPATCHER-01`. The events a transition may append: every kind but ``assigned``.

CreateAssignmentRequest.title: CreateAssignmentRequest
CreateAssignmentRequest.description: `W61-DISPATCHER-01`. Give a project, or one document of it, to an active expert.

TransitionAssignmentRequest.title: TransitionAssignmentRequest
TransitionAssignmentRequest.description: `W61-DISPATCHER-01`. One move along an assignment's history.

Assignment.title: Assignment
Assignment.description: `W61-DISPATCHER-01`. One assignment as it now stands.

AssignmentDetail.title: AssignmentDetail
AssignmentDetail.description: `W61-DISPATCHER-01`. One assignment and its whole history, oldest event first.

EffectiveVendorLists.title: EffectiveVendorLists
EffectiveVendorLists.description: All fifteen sections' vendor lists as they apply to one project, in section order.

PriceListAmbiguousColumn.title: PriceListAmbiguousColumn
PriceListAmbiguousColumn.description: An optional field two or more columns could be: none of them was read.

PriceListColumn.title: PriceListColumn
PriceListColumn.description: One header column mapped to a field: its 1-based position and its header text.

PriceListCurrencySource.title: PriceListCurrencySource
PriceListCurrencySource.description: Where an accepted row's currency came from: its cell, the price header, the default.

PriceListField.title: PriceListField
PriceListField.description: A position field a header column was mapped to.

PriceListFormat.title: PriceListFormat
PriceListFormat.description: The uploaded file's format, recognised by its bytes and never by its name.

PriceListParseReport.title: PriceListParseReport

PriceListPosition.title: PriceListPosition
PriceListPosition.description: One parsed position. ``row_number`` is its source row, never an identity.

PriceListPositionPage.title: PriceListPositionPage
PriceListPositionPage.description: One page of a revision's positions in source-row order, with the revision's report.

PriceListRevision.title: PriceListRevision

PriceListRevisionList.title: PriceListRevisionList
PriceListRevisionList.description: Every price-list revision of one project, newest first; the first one is current.

PriceListRowNote.title: PriceListRowNote
PriceListRowNote.description: One source row (as the spreadsheet numbers it) and why it is reported.

PriceListRowReason.title: PriceListRowReason
PriceListRowReason.description:
Why a data row was skipped (the first ten), or a warning on an accepted row (the last).

A skipped row is never repaired: a price that is not a plain number, not positive, finer
than six decimals or not below 10^14 is reported, never guessed or rounded.

SectionVendorList.title: SectionVendorList
SectionVendorList.description: One section's vendor list as it applies to a project, with both scopes' latest.

SetGlobalVendorListRequest.title: SetGlobalVendorListRequest
SetGlobalVendorListRequest.description:
`W60-PRICE-LIST-01`. A section's global vendor list, as a whole new revision.

``expected_vendor_list_id``, when present, is the revision the caller read (``null``:
there was none); a different latest revision is ``conflict`` and nothing is written.

SetProjectVendorListRequest.title: SetProjectVendorListRequest
SetProjectVendorListRequest.description:
`W60-PRICE-LIST-01`. A project's own vendor list for a section, or its removal.

``mode: inherit`` takes ``entries: []`` and removes the override. ``expected_vendor_list_id``
as for :class:`SetGlobalVendorListRequest`, for this project's revisions.

UploadPriceListRequest.title: UploadPriceListRequest
UploadPriceListRequest.description:
`W60-PRICE-LIST-01`. The multipart body of ``uploadPriceList``.

``file`` is the price list (CSV, or an XLSX whose first sheet is read), at most 10 MiB;
``default_currency`` applies to rows whose currency neither their own cell nor the price
column's header names.

VendorListEntry.title: VendorListEntry
VendorListEntry.description: One entry: the material or equipment group it covers, the allowed vendor, a note.

VendorListMode.title: VendorListMode
VendorListMode.description:
``list``: these entries apply (none at all is an explicit "no restriction").
``inherit``: a project revision that removes the override; the global list applies.

VendorListRevision.title: VendorListRevision
VendorListRevision.description: One immutable revision of a section's vendor list, global or of one project.

VendorListSource.title: VendorListSource
VendorListSource.description: Which revision applies to a project's section: its own list, the global one, or none.

SpecificationPriceListRef.title: SpecificationPriceListRef
SpecificationPriceListRef.description: The price-list revision the rows were matched against: the project's current one.

SpecificationSkipCounts.title: SpecificationSkipCounts
SpecificationSkipCounts.description: Lines inside detected tables that became neither a row nor part of one, by reason.

SpecificationSkippedLine.title: SpecificationSkippedLine
SpecificationSkippedLine.description: One skipped line: where it is, why, and the start of its text.

SpecificationTable.title: SpecificationTable
SpecificationTable.description: One detected specification table: its header lines and the Form-7 columns it names.

SpecificationExtractionSummary.title: SpecificationExtractionSummary
SpecificationExtractionSummary.description: What the extractor found: counts complete, listings capped at 200 each.

SpecificationExclusionCounts.title: SpecificationExclusionCounts
SpecificationExclusionCounts.description: Rows left out of every total, by the one reason each carries.

SpecificationCurrencyTotal.title: SpecificationCurrencyTotal
SpecificationCurrencyTotal.description: The exact sum of the amounts in one currency; never converted, never rounded.

SpecificationMatching.title: SpecificationMatching
SpecificationMatching.description: Every row's match counted, the totals per currency and what they leave out.

SpecificationPricePosition.title: SpecificationPricePosition
SpecificationPricePosition.description: The one price-list position a row is matched to, as the price list states it.

SpecificationPriceRow.title: SpecificationPriceRow
SpecificationPriceRow.description: One specification row and its match. ``amount`` only when it counts in a total.

SpecificationRowPage.title: SpecificationRowPage
SpecificationRowPage.description: One page of the rows; the counts and totals always cover every row.

SpecificationPrices.title: SpecificationPrices
SpecificationPrices.description:
The priced specification of a set's current version, or the state that stops it.

The states are checked in order -- ``version_unclassified``, ``section_not_ar``,
``price_list_missing``, ``analysis_missing``, ``text_unavailable``,
``specification_too_large`` -- and each answer carries the facts read before it stopped. ``section_not_ar`` is kept so that no
value is removed, but it is no longer produced: a version confirmed in any of the fifteen
sections is read.

DecideOptimisationProposalRequest.title: DecideOptimisationProposalRequest
DecideOptimisationProposalRequest.description:
`W60-OPT-PROPOSALS-01`. An expert's verdict on a proposal, with a comment that
``revise`` requires.

OptimisationPass.title: OptimisationPass
OptimisationPass.description:
One optimisation pass, pinned to everything it read: the version, its published run
and that run's text layer, the price-list revision and the vendor-list revision (global
or the project's own, ``vendor_list_source``), and the three algorithm versions.

OptimisationProposal.title: OptimisationProposal
OptimisationProposal.description:
One proposal: a specification row matched to ``matched_position`` and a cheaper
``proposed_position`` of the same price-list revision, in the same unit and currency,
from a vendor on the pass's vendor list.

``row_text`` is the description as the saved text layer shows it (name, mark, code and
manufacturer cells run together); page, sheet and lines say where it is. Both unit prices
are the positions' stored prices. ``saving`` is ``(current_unit_price −
proposed_unit_price) × quantity`` and is ``null`` -- never ``0`` -- when ``quantity`` is
``null`` because the row's quantity text is not a plain number. ``ordinal`` is a display
order inside the pass, never an identity.

OptimisationProposalPage.title: OptimisationProposalPage
OptimisationProposalPage.description:
One page of a pass's proposals in ordinal order. ``total`` counts the proposals the
``decision`` filter admits; the pass's ``decision_counts`` count all of them.

OptimisationProposalType.title: OptimisationProposalType
OptimisationProposalType.description:
The kind of a proposal. Only the deterministic one exists: a cheaper position of the
same price list. The legacy ``faster_install``, ``simpler_design`` and ``lifecycle`` need
judgement and wait for the model-assisted slice.

ProposalAnalogBasis.title: ProposalAnalogBasis
ProposalAnalogBasis.description:
Why the proposed position is the same kind of product: one code family (the leading
letters of the code or mark, ``ПК 60-12-8`` ~ ``ПК 63-15-8``), or at least half of the
words of the two names in common.

ProposalDecision.title: ProposalDecision
ProposalDecision.description: One appended expert decision. Never changed; the proposal's latest one is current.

ProposalDecisionCounts.title: ProposalDecisionCounts
ProposalDecisionCounts.description:
How many of a pass's proposals stand in each decision state; the four sum to the
pass's ``proposal_count``. These are the proposals' own counts, never finding counts.

ProposalDecisionList.title: ProposalDecisionList
ProposalDecisionList.description: Every decision of one proposal, oldest first; the last is current.

ProposalDecisionResult.title: ProposalDecisionResult
ProposalDecisionResult.description: The decision appended (or replayed) and the proposal as it now stands.

ProposalDecisionState.title: ProposalDecisionState
ProposalDecisionState.description:
A proposal's current decision: its latest verdict, or ``pending`` when nobody decided.
Also the ``decision`` filter of ``listOptimisationProposals``.

ProposalMatchBasis.title: ProposalMatchBasis
ProposalMatchBasis.description: How the specification row was matched to its current price-list position.

ProposalPosition.title: ProposalPosition
ProposalPosition.description:
A price-list position a proposal names. ``row_number`` is its source row, never an
identity.

ProposalVerdict.title: ProposalVerdict
ProposalVerdict.description:
An expert's verdict on a proposal. ``revise`` says the analog is right in principle
and the proposal needs changing; its comment is required.

SectionSpecificationSource.title: SectionSpecificationSource
SectionSpecificationSource.description:
One document set whose current version is confirmed in the section, and how far it read.

``state`` is ``ready`` when the saved text was read and the rows extracted;
``analysis_missing`` (no published run) and ``text_unavailable`` (a run without a saved
text layer) name what is missing; ``specification_too_large`` is the extractor's own row
bound; ``not_read`` is a set the answer did not read because it is over a bound
(``SectionSpecification.limit_reason``). The extraction facts are ``null`` until read.

SectionSpecificationProject.title: SectionSpecificationProject
SectionSpecificationProject.description:
One project with member sets: its price list, its sets and its own totals.

``price_state`` is ``priced`` (the current price-list revision was read), ``price_list_missing``
(none uploaded: the rows are served without any match and no figure) or ``not_read`` (over a
bound). ``matching`` covers this project's rows only and is ``null`` unless ``priced``; its
totals are per currency and never mixed with another project's.

SectionSpecificationExcludedVersion.title: SectionSpecificationExcludedVersion
SectionSpecificationExcludedVersion.description: A current version that cannot be placed in a section yet: nobody classified it.

SectionSpecificationRow.title: SectionSpecificationRow
SectionSpecificationRow.description:
One Form-7 row with its full address and, where the project has a price list, its match.

``price_status`` is the match (``matched``, ``ambiguous``, ``unmatched``) or
``price_list_missing`` when the row's project has no price list: then every match field is
empty and no price or amount exists. ``amount`` only when the row counts in its project's
total for its currency.

SectionSpecificationRowPage.title: SectionSpecificationRowPage
SectionSpecificationRowPage.description: One page of the rows that survive the text search; the counts cover every row.

SectionSpecification.title: SectionSpecification
SectionSpecification.description:
The combined Form-7 specification of one section, project by project.

``state`` is ``ready`` or ``section_too_large`` with ``limit_reason`` naming the bound that
stopped it (``projects`` scanned, member ``sources`` read, ``rows`` held); then the
membership is still listed with every set ``not_read`` and ``rows`` is ``null`` -- narrowing
to one project (``project_filter``) is the way in. ``excluded`` lists the current versions
nobody classified (the first 200; ``excluded_count`` is complete). ``row_count`` counts
every row in scope and ``rows.total`` the rows the text search keeps. There is no section
total: the totals live in each project's ``matching``.

NormReferenceCounts.description: Distinct cited designations per outcome; every outcome is present, zeros written.

NormReferenceAnchor.description: One occurrence of a citation: the PDF page and the offsets inside that page's text.

NormReferenceItem.description: One distinct cited designation and what the pinned snapshot holds for it. `anchors` keeps at most ten occurrences in reading order; `occurrence_count` is the true number. The `matched_*` properties name the corpus document the outcome points at (the same edition, the newer one, or the newest earlier one) and are absent exactly for `not_in_corpus` and `not_recognised`. `matched_designation` and `matched_title` are derived for display from the stored file name and are never identities.
